And [[5:3|his father answered him|Respondit ei pater]]: [[5:3|I have a note of his hand with me|Chirographum illius penes me habeo]]: when he has seen it, he will pay thee back, that is, he will pay the money in full.

paras.t: Tunc egressus Tobias, invenit juvenem splendidum stantem præcinctum, id est angelum in forma juvenis speciosi, quasi paratum ad ambulandum. Et quod ait, Quasi, designat hic veritatem, non similitudinem tantum, quemadmodum apud Joannem, dum dicitur: Vidimus gloriam ejus, gloriam quasi Unigeniti a Patre.
paras.en: [[5:5|Then Tobias going forth, found a beautiful young man, standing girded|Tunc egressus Tobias, invenit juvenem splendidum stantem præcinctum]], that is, an angel in the form of a comely young man, [[5:5|as it were ready to walk|quasi paratum ad ambulandum]]. And where it says [[5:5|as it were|Quasi]], this signifies here the reality, not only a likeness, as in John, where it is said: [[John 1:14|we saw his glory, the glory as it were of the only begotten of the Father|Vidimus gloriam ejus, gloriam quasi Unigeniti a Patre]].

paras.t: Circa hoc scribit quidam: Apparitiones angelicæ in assumptis corporibus fiunt secundum proprietates legationum, ad quas angeli mittuntur. Et quoniam iste mittebatur a Deo ad ducendum filium Tobiæ per viam, apparuit tanquam dispositus ad itinerandum. Quod quamvis aliquando ita sit, præsertim dum angeli mox volunt ipso apparatu ostendere ad quid venerint, non tamen videtur semper sic factum. Legitur enim in Genesi, qualiter duo angeli missi ad Sodomam subvertendam, ingressi sint in domum Lot: qui angeli apparuerunt in forma valde gratiosa atque amabili, non vehementer terribili. Propter quod cives Sodomæ æstimantes quod essent pulcherrimi juvenes, venerunt ut eis abuterentur. Et si apparuissent secundum proprietatem et habitudinem suæ legationis, apparuissent utique in forma metuenda, velut commoti. In libro Judicum quoque mater Samsonis legitur marito suo dixisse de angelo: Vir Dei venit ad me, habens vultum angelicum, terribilis nimis. Et tamen angelus ille venit ad prænuntiandum valde jucunda et prospera: sicque, secundum dictum prætactum, apparuisset in forma hilari et amœna, non ita terrifica. Simili modo argui posset de angelo qui apparuit Cornelio centurioni in forma terribili, ut patet in Actibus: atque de angelis qui (ut Evangelistæ describunt) nuntiaverunt Christi resurrectionem mulieribus sanctis, quibus in specie apparuerunt terribili.
paras.en: On this a certain writer says: The apparitions of angels in assumed bodies take place according to the character of the embassies on which the angels are sent. And since this angel was sent by God to lead the son of Tobias on his way, he appeared as one made ready for a journey. Now although this is so at times, above all when angels wish to show at once by their very array what they have come for, yet it does not seem always to have been done so. For we read in Genesis how the two angels sent to overthrow Sodom went into the house of Lot[[Gen 19:1||]]; and these angels appeared in a form most gracious and lovable, not at all terrible. For this reason the citizens of Sodom, thinking them very beautiful young men, came to abuse them. Yet had they appeared according to the character and bearing of their embassy, they would surely have appeared in a fearful form, as if roused to wrath. In the book of Judges, too, we read that the mother of Samson said to her husband of the angel: [[Judg 13:6|A man of God came to me, having the countenance of an angel, very awful|Vir Dei venit ad me, habens vultum angelicum, terribilis nimis]]. And yet that angel came to foretell things most joyful and prosperous; and so, by the saying touched on above, he would have appeared in a cheerful and pleasant form, not so terrifying. The same argument could be made from the angel who appeared to Cornelius the centurion in a terrible form, as is plain in the Acts[[Acts 10:3||]][[Acts 10:4||]]; and from the angels who (as the Evangelists describe) announced the resurrection of Christ to the holy women, and appeared to them in a terrible guise[[Matt 28:2||]][[Mark 16:5||]][[Luke 24:4||]][[John 20:12||]].

paras.t: Et dixit Tobias junior ad angelum: Unde te habemus, bone juvenis? hoc est, de qua natione et terra es tu? Optavit enim aliquem filiorum Israel habere ducem sui itineris. At ille respondit: Ex filiis Israel: quod verum est, secundum nominis interpretationem. Israel quippe interpretatur, videns Deum: sicque fuit ex filiis Israel, hoc est de numero filiorum contemplantium Deum, de quibus in Job Dominus ait: Quum me laudarent astra matutina, et jubilarent omnes filii Dei. Unde in Deuteronomio, ubi habemus, Constituit terminos populorum, juxta numerum filiorum Israel: alia translatio habet, Statuit terminos gentium, juxta numerum angelorum Dei.
paras.en: And the younger Tobias said to the angel: [[5:6|From whence art thou, good young man?|Unde te habemus, bone juvenis?]] that is, of what nation and land art thou? For he wished to have one of the children of Israel as the guide of his journey. [[5:7|But he answered: Of the children of Israel|At ille respondit: Ex filiis Israel]]: which is true, according to the interpretation of the name. For Israel is interpreted "seeing God"; and so he was of the children of Israel, that is, of the number of the sons who contemplate God, of whom the Lord says in Job: [[Job 38:7|When the morning stars praised me together, and all the sons of God made a joyful melody?|Quum me laudarent astra matutina, et jubilarent omnes filii Dei]] Hence in Deuteronomy, where we have, [[Deut 32:8|he appointed the bounds of people according to the number of the children of Israel|Constituit terminos populorum, juxta numerum filiorum Israel]], another translation [that is, the Septuagint] has: He set the bounds of the nations according to the number of the angels of God.

paras.t: Et Tobias dixit ei: Nosti viam quæ ducit in regionem Medorum? Cui respondit: Novi; et omnia itinera ejus frequenter ambulavi, et mansi apud Gabelum fratrem nostrum, qui moratur in Rages civitate Medorum, quæ posita est in monte Ecbatanis. Ex quo elicitur, quod Gabelus fuit vir justus: propter quod angelus sanctus invisibiliter sæpius adfuit ei et libenter: quem nominat fratrem propter caritatis communionem, et gratiam gratificantem, et quia (ut creditur) fuit de numero electorum; itemque, propter convenientiam in natura intellectuali, saltem in genere, et quia eumdem habebant Patrem cœlestem. Sic et in Apocalypsi angelus ait Joanni: Conservus tuus sum. Cui Tobias ait: Sustine me, obsecro, donec hæc ipsa nuntiem patri meo.
paras.en: [[5:7|And Tobias said to him: Knowest thou the way that leadeth to the country of the Medes?|Et Tobias dixit ei: Nosti viam quæ ducit in regionem Medorum?]] [[5:8|And he answered|Cui respondit]]: [[5:8|I know it: and I have often walked through all the ways thereof, and I have abode with Gabelus our brother, who dwelleth at Rages a city of the Medes, which is situate in the mount of Ecbatana|Novi; et omnia itinera ejus frequenter ambulavi, et mansi apud Gabelum fratrem nostrum, qui moratur in Rages civitate Medorum, quæ posita est in monte Ecbatanis]]. From this it is gathered that Gabelus was a just man, and for that reason the holy angel was often present with him, unseen, and gladly; and he calls him brother because of their fellowship in charity and sanctifying grace [gratia gratificans, the grace that makes a man pleasing to God], and because (as is believed) he was of the number of the elect; and also because they agree in an intellectual nature, at least in kind, and because they had the same heavenly Father. So too in the Apocalypse the angel says to John: [[Apoc 19:10|I am thy fellow servant|Conservus tuus sum]]. [[5:9|And Tobias said to him: Stay for me, I beseech thee, till I tell these same things to my father|Cui Tobias ait: Sustine me, obsecro, donec hæc ipsa nuntiem patri meo]].

paras.t: Tunc ingressus Tobias, indicavit universa hæc patri suo. Super quæ admiratus pater, rogavit ut introiret ad eum. Ingressus itaque angelus domum Tobiæ senioris, salutavit eum, et dixit: Gaudium tibi semper sit, id est spiritualis in Deo jucunditas: in quo gloriandum est, non in prosperis tantum, sed etiam, imo et potius in adversis. Unde hortatur Apostolus: Gaudete in Domino semper.
paras.en: [[5:10|Then Tobias going in told all these things to his father. Upon which his father being in admiration, desired that he would come in unto him|Tunc ingressus Tobias, indicavit universa hæc patri suo. Super quæ admiratus pater, rogavit ut introiret ad eum]]. [[5:11|So going in|Ingressus itaque]] to the house of the elder Tobias, the angel [[5:11|saluted him, and said: Joy be to thee always|salutavit eum, et dixit: Gaudium tibi semper sit]], that is, spiritual delight in God, in whom we must glory not only in prosperity but also, nay rather, in adversity. Hence the Apostle exhorts: [[Phil 4:4|Rejoice in the Lord always|Gaudete in Domino semper]].

paras.t: Et Tobias ait: Quale mihi gaudium erit in sæculo isto? quasi dicat: Carnale et sæculare gaudium non convenit mihi, neque id opto; qui in tenebris sedeo, et lumen cæli non video, id est solem et ejus splendorem, quum in Ecclesiaste scriptum sit: Dulce lumen, et delectabile oculis videre solem. Et forsan de hujusmodi gaudio putavit Tobias angelum, tanquam juvenem hominem, esse locutum. Cui ait juvenis, id est angelus in juvenis forma apparens, qui nunquam antiquatur, sed in suo vigore incorruptibiliter invariabiliterque permanet: Forti animo esto, id est constans, non desolatus. In proximo est, ut a Deo cureris per ministerium meum a plaga cæcitatis. Hoc prædixit ei in generali: quod tamen Tobias non multum ponderans, ad alia se convertit.
paras.en: [[5:12|And Tobias said: What manner of joy shall be to me|Et Tobias ait: Quale mihi gaudium erit]] in this world? As if to say: Carnal and worldly joy does not befit me, nor do I wish for it, [[5:12|who sit in darkness and see not the light of heaven?|qui in tenebris sedeo, et lumen cæli non video]] that is, the sun and its brightness; for it is written in Ecclesiastes: [[Eccles 11:7|The light is sweet, and it is delightful for the eyes to see the sun|Dulce lumen, et delectabile oculis videre solem]]. And perhaps Tobias thought that the angel, as a young man, had spoken of joy of that kind. [[5:13|And the young man said to him|Cui ait juvenis]], that is, the angel appearing in the form of a young man, who never grows old but abides in his vigour incorruptibly and unchangeably: [[5:13|Be of good courage|Forti animo esto]], that is, steadfast, not desolate; [[5:13|thy cure from God is at hand|In proximo est, ut a Deo cureris]], by my ministry, from the affliction of blindness. This he foretold to him in general terms; but Tobias, not weighing it much, turned to other things.

paras.t: Dixitque illi Tobias: Numquid poteris perducere filium meum ad Gabelum in Rages civitatem Medorum? Et quum redieris, restituam tibi mercedem tuam. Et angelus: Ego ducam et reducam eum. Cui Tobias: Rogo te, indica mihi de qua domo, id est familia, aut tribu es tu: quia in una tribu erant plures familiæ, ut patet in Numeris. Tamen in tribu Dan, erat tantum una familia: quia Dan filius Jacob, unum dumtaxat habuit filium, ut in Genesi habetur.
paras.en: [[5:14|And Tobias said to him: Canst thou conduct my son to Gabelus at Rages, a city of the Medes? and when thou shalt return, I will pay thee thy hire|Dixitque illi Tobias: Numquid poteris perducere filium meum ad Gabelum in Rages civitatem Medorum? Et quum redieris, restituam tibi mercedem tuam]]. [[5:15|And the angel|Et angelus]]: [[5:15|I will conduct him thither, and bring him back|Ego ducam et reducam eum]]. [[5:16|And Tobias said to him|Cui Tobias]]: [[5:16|I pray thee, tell me, of what family|Rogo te, indica mihi de qua domo]] [domus, literally "house"], that is, kindred, [[5:16|or what tribe art thou|aut tribu es tu]]: for in one tribe there were several families, as is plain in Numbers[[Num 26:1||]]. But in the tribe of Dan there was only one family, because Dan the son of Jacob had only one son, as we have in Genesis[[Gen 46:23||]].

paras.t: Cui Raphael dixit: Genus, id est stirpem, quæris mercenarii, an ipsum mercenarium qui cum filio tuo eat? quasi dicat: Plus quæris, quam ad præsens spectat negotium, quia sufficere tibi potest, ut certificeris de fidelitate ductoris filii tui, nec opus est genealogiam ejus agnoscere. Sed ne forte sollicitum te reddam, hoc est immoderate anxium, non respondendo, ego sum Azarias Ananiæ magni filius. Quæ responsio vera est, secundum nominis interpretationem et figurativam locutionem. Azarias namque interpretatur, adjutor Dei; Ananias vero, gratia seu gloria Dei. Fuit itaque Azarias, hoc est adjutor Dei, id est, per quem Deus adjuvit Tobiam ac alios multos. Juxta quem modum ait Apostolus: Dei adjutores sumus. Fuit quoque filius Ananiæ magni, hoc est filius gratiæ et gloriæ summi Dei. Juxta hunc sensum exponit Hieronymus, quod Zacharias a Judæis lapidatus inter templum et altare, vocatur filius Barachiæ, quum fuerit filius Joiadæ. Porro, ea quæ angeli inter homines loquuntur et agunt, sæpe sunt figurativa; et quamvis nunquam mentiantur, veritatem tamen interdum occultant.
paras.en: [[5:17|And Raphael the angel answered|Cui Raphael dixit]]: [[5:17|Dost thou seek the family|Genus]], that is, the stock, [[5:17|of him thou hirest, or the hired servant himself to go with thy son?|quæris mercenarii, an ipsum mercenarium qui cum filio tuo eat?]] As if to say: Thou askest more than the present business concerns, for it can be enough for thee to be made sure of the faithfulness of thy son's guide, and there is no need to know his genealogy. [[5:18|But lest I should make thee uneasy|Sed ne forte sollicitum te reddam]], that is, immoderately anxious, by not answering, [[5:18|I am Azarias the son of the great Ananias|ego sum Azarias Ananiæ magni filius]]. This answer is true according to the interpretation of the names and a figurative way of speaking. For Azarias is interpreted "helper of God", and Ananias "grace" or "glory of God". So he was Azarias, that is, a helper of God, one through whom God helped Tobias and many others; in which way the Apostle says: [[1 Cor 3:9|we are God's coadjutors|Dei adjutores sumus]] [adjutores, "helpers", the word Denis has just used to interpret Azarias]. He was also the son of the great Ananias, that is, a son of the grace and glory of the most high God. In this sense Jerome explains that Zacharias, stoned by the Jews between the temple and the altar[[2 Par 24:20||]], is called the son of Barachias, though he was the son of Joiada [Christ calls him so at Matt 23:35; Barachias is taken to mean "blessed of the Lord"]. Moreover, what angels say and do among men is often figurative; and although they never lie, yet they sometimes hide the truth.

paras.t: Et Tobias respondit: Ex magno genere es tu. Quod verum est, quia ex genere ac specie angelorum a Deo omnipotente immediate creatorum, quamvis non fuerit verum, prout Tobias tunc intellexit; nec tamen mentiebatur formaliter, quia non intendebat falsum proferre, neque decipere. Sed peto ne irascaris quod voluerim cognoscere genus tuum. Dixit illi angelus: Ego sanum ducam et reducam tibi filium tuum. Respondens autem Tobias, ait: Bene ambuletis, et sit Dominus in itinere vestro, et angelus ejus comitetur vobiscum, hoc est, comes et socius vester sit in vestro itinere: quemadmodum Dominus ait in Exodo ad Moysen, Angelus meus præcedet te.
paras.en: [[5:19|And Tobias answered: Thou art of a great family|Et Tobias respondit: Ex magno genere es tu]]. Which is true, for he was of the family and species of the angels, created immediately by almighty God; though it was not true in the way Tobias then understood it. Yet he was not lying formally [that is, telling a lie in the proper sense, which needs the will to say what is false], because he did not intend to utter a falsehood or to deceive. [[5:19|But I pray thee be not angry that I desired to know thy family|Sed peto ne irascaris quod voluerim cognoscere genus tuum]]. [[5:20|And the angel said to him|Dixit illi angelus]]: [[5:20|I will lead thy son safe, and bring him to thee again safe|Ego sanum ducam et reducam tibi filium tuum]]. [[5:21|And Tobias answering, said: May you have a good journey, and God be with you in your way, and his angel accompany you|Respondens autem Tobias, ait: Bene ambuletis, et sit Dominus in itinere vestro, et angelus ejus comitetur vobiscum]], that is, be your companion and fellow on your journey; as the Lord says to Moses in Exodus: [[Ex 23:23|And my angel shall go before thee|Angelus meus præcedet te]] [the margin gives Exod. xxiii, 23; Denis's words are exactly those of Ex 32:34].

paras.t: Tunc paratis omnibus quæ erant in via portanda, dixit Tobias, Vale, patri suo et matri suæ, et ambulaverunt ambo simul, hoc est, parentibus suis valefecit, recedendo ab eis.
paras.en: [[5:22|Then all things being ready, that were to be carried in their journey|Tunc paratis omnibus quæ erant in via portanda]], Tobias said Farewell to his father and his mother [the Vulgate has fecit vale, "bade farewell"; Denis reads dixit Vale, "said Farewell"], [[5:22|and they set out both together|et ambulaverunt ambo simul]]: that is, he took leave of his parents as he went away from them.

paras.t: Quumque profecti essent angelus et Tobias, cœpit flere mater ejus et dicere. Feminæ enim ad fletum communiter pronæ sunt; et statim ut mater Tobiæ destitutam se sensit tam dilecti et amabilis filii adspectu suavi, cœpit affligi. Baculum senectutis nostræ tulisti, et (pro id est) transmisisti a nobis, hoc est unicum et carissimum filium nostrum, cui in hoc senio innitebamur, tanquam baculo in necessitatibus nostris, qui fuit nobis in solatium et obsequium. Utinam nunquam fuisset ipsa pecunia, pro qua misisti eum, hoc est, utinam nunquam fuisset, neque ad nos pertinuisset pecunia illa, quæ fit nobis tantæ afflictionis et mœroris occasio. Sufficiebat enim nobis paupertas nostra, ut divitias computaremus hoc, quod videbamus filium nostrum: hoc est, sufficientius ac tolerabilius nobis esse debuerat, quod habuimus filium nostrum sensibiliter nobis præsentem, cum exterioris substantiæ seu pecuniæ mutuatæ carentia, quam emissio ista filii nostri pro acquirenda pecunia.
paras.en: [[5:23|And when they were departed|Quumque profecti essent]], the angel and Tobias, [[5:23|his mother began to weep, and to say|cœpit flere mater ejus et dicere]]. For women are commonly prone to weeping; and as soon as the mother of Tobias felt herself bereft of the sweet sight of so dear and lovable a son, she began to be afflicted. [[5:23|Thou hast taken the staff of our old age|Baculum senectutis nostræ tulisti]], and (put for "that is") [[5:23|sent him away from us|transmisisti a nobis]]: that is, our only and dearest son, on whom we leaned in this old age as on a staff in our needs, and who was our comfort and our service. [[5:24|I wish the money for which thou hast sent him, had never been|Utinam nunquam fuisset ipsa pecunia, pro qua misisti eum]]: that is, would that that money had never been, nor had belonged to us, which is to us the occasion of so great affliction and grief. [[5:25|For our poverty was sufficient for us, that we might account it as riches, that we saw our son|Sufficiebat enim nobis paupertas nostra, ut divitias computaremus hoc, quod videbamus filium nostrum]]: that is, it ought to have been more sufficient and more bearable to us to have our son present to our senses, with the want of outward substance, that is, of the money lent, than this sending away of our son to recover the money.

paras.t: Denique, quamvis [vir ejus] jam erat cæcus, pluraliter tamen dixit, Quod videbamus, juxta modum loquendi, quo societati adscribitur, quod convenit parti ipsius. Vel quod ait, Videbamus, intelligi potest de corporali intuitu, quantum ad Annam, et de visu imaginario ac intellectuali, quantum ad cæcum Tobiam, cui delectabile fuit, quod filium suum vere imaginabatur ac intellexit præsentialiter sibi adesse. Visus quoque interdum pro aliis exterioribus sensibus sumitur. Unde communiter dicitur: Vide quam bene hoc sapiat seu odoret. In Apocalypsi quoque ait S. Joannes: Conversus sum, ut viderem vocem quæ loquebatur mecum. In Exodo item legitur: Populus videbat voces, hoc est, audiebat.
paras.en: Further, although her husband was already blind, she still said in the plural, [[5:25|that we saw|Quod videbamus]], after the manner of speaking by which what belongs to a part of a company is ascribed to the company. Or the words [[5:25|we saw|Videbamus]] can be understood of bodily sight as regards Anna, and of imaginative and intellectual vision as regards the blind Tobias, to whom it was a delight that he truly pictured his son and understood him to be present with him. Sight, too, is sometimes taken for the other outward senses; hence it is commonly said: See how well this tastes, or smells. In the Apocalypse also St. John says: [[Apoc 1:12|I turned to see the voice that spoke with me|Conversus sum, ut viderem vocem quæ loquebatur mecum]]. And in Exodus we read: [[Ex 20:18|the people saw the voices|Populus videbat voces]], that is, heard them.

paras.t: Dixitque ei Tobias, conjugem consolando. Virorum enim est uxores instruere, quia vir caput est uxoris, et communiter fortiores in ratione, constantioresque mente sunt viri quam feminæ. Et præsertim Tobias multo virtuosior ac sapientior fuit conjuge sua. Noli flere. Salvus perveniet filius noster, et salvus revertetur ad nos, et oculi tui videbunt illum. Hoc fuit verbum bonum spei, non tamen certitudinis absolutæ. Ideo addit: Credo quod angelus Dei bonus comitetur ei, et bene disponat omnia quæ circa eum geruntur, id est, director et protector sit ejus, ita ut cum gaudio revertatur ad nos. Ad hanc vocem cessavit mater ejus flere, et tacuit.
paras.en: [[5:26|And Tobias said to her|Dixitque ei Tobias]], consoling his wife. For it is for husbands to instruct their wives, because [[Eph 5:23|the husband is the head of the wife|vir caput est uxoris]], and men are commonly stronger in reason and steadier in mind than women; and Tobias above all was far more virtuous and wiser than his wife. [[5:26|Weep not, our son will arrive thither safe, and will return safe to us, and thy eyes shall see him|Noli flere. Salvus perveniet filius noster, et salvus revertetur ad nos, et oculi tui videbunt illum]]. This was a good word of hope, but not of absolute certainty. Therefore he adds: [[5:27|I believe that the good angel of God doth accompany him, and doth order all things well that are done about him|Credo quod angelus Dei bonus comitetur ei, et bene disponat omnia quæ circa eum geruntur]], that is, is his director and protector, [[5:27|so that he shall return to us with joy|ita ut cum gaudio revertatur ad nos]]. [[5:28|At these words his mother ceased weeping, and held her peace|Ad hanc vocem cessavit mater ejus flere, et tacuit]].

6.title: Elucidatio capituli sexti: Profectus est autem Tobias, et canis secutus est eum
6.title_en: Explanation of the sixth chapter: And Tobias went forward, and the dog followed him

paras.t: Exordium itinerationis Tobiæ hic enarratur, et qualiter in ea ereptus sit a periculo mortis, et informatus de remediis contra aliquas plagas, atque præavisatus de uxore accipienda.
paras.en: Here is told the beginning of Tobias's journey, and how on it he was rescued from the danger of death, and instructed in remedies against certain afflictions, and forewarned about the wife he was to take.

paras.t: Profectus est autem Tobias cum angelo, et canis secutus est eum: quod tangi videtur, ad innuendum quod erat pius, etiam circa brutum, et liberalis, dando alimoniam ei; et mansit prima mansione, id est dieta, in hospitio juxta fluvium Tigri, qui est unus de quatuor fluminibus paradisi, per terram Assyriorum decurrens, ut in Genesi habetur. Et exivit de hospitio ut lavaret pedes suos, pro mitigatione laboris peregrinationis. Et ecce piscis immanis, id est magnus, crudelis, inhumanus, exivit de fluvio. Aliqui enim pisces extra aquam ad tempus perdurant, jacent, decurrunt, ut crocodili, suntque quadrupedes. Ad devorandum eum. Sic et Hieronymus primo libro Vitarum Patrum, describens pericula viæ suæ, recitat qualiter crocodili cucurrerunt post eum et socios suos ad devorandum.
paras.en: [[6:1|And Tobias went forward|Profectus est autem Tobias]] with the angel, [[6:1|and the dog followed him|et canis secutus est eum]]: which seems to be mentioned to suggest that he was kind even towards a brute beast, and generous in giving it food; [[6:1|and he lodged the first night|et mansit prima mansione]], that is, the first day's journey [Latin *mansio*, a stopping-place or a day's stage, which Denis glosses with *dieta*, a day's journey], at an inn [[6:1|by the river of Tigris|juxta fluvium Tigri]], which is one of the four rivers of paradise, running through the land of the Assyrians, as is had in Genesis[[Gen 2:14||]]. [[6:2|And he went out|Et exivit]] from the inn [[6:2|to wash his feet|ut lavaret pedes suos]], to ease the toil of the journey. [[6:2|and behold a monstrous fish|Et ecce piscis immanis]], that is, great, cruel, savage, [[6:2|came up|exivit de fluvio]] from the river. For some fishes last for a time out of the water, lie and run about, as crocodiles do, and they are four-footed. [[6:2|to devour him|Ad devorandum eum]]. So too Jerome, in the first book of the Lives of the Fathers, describing the dangers of his journey, relates how crocodiles ran after him and his companions to devour them.

paras.t: Quem expavescens Tobias, clamavit voce magna, dicens: Domine, invadit me. Sicque ductorem suum in periculo dominum nominavit, ut sibi tanquam servo succurreret. Et dixit ei angelus: Apprehende branchiam ejus, hoc est locum seu pennulam exsistentem inter caput et corpus piscis, et trahe eum ad te. Quod quum fecisset, attraxit eum in siccum, et palpitare cœpit ante pedes ejus. Mirum quod facere hoc audebat: sed Deus confortavit eum intrinsecus, similiter angelus apparatu mirifico.
paras.en: [[6:3|And Tobias being afraid of him, cried out with a loud voice|Quem expavescens Tobias, clamavit voce magna]], [[6:3|saying: Sir, he cometh upon me|dicens: Domine, invadit me]]. And so in his danger he called his guide lord [Latin *Domine*, which the Douay-Rheims renders “Sir”], so that he would help him as his servant. [[6:4|And the angel said to him: Take him by the gill|Et dixit ei angelus: Apprehende branchiam ejus]], that is, the place or little fin that lies between the head and the body of the fish, [[6:4|and draw him to thee|et trahe eum ad te]]. [[6:4|And when he had done so, he drew him out upon the land, and he began to pant before his feet|Quod quum fecisset, attraxit eum in siccum, et palpitare cœpit ante pedes ejus]]. It is a wonder that he dared to do this: but God strengthened him inwardly, and likewise the angel by a wonderful provision.

paras.t: Tunc dixit angelus: Exentera hunc piscem, id est, interiora seu intestina ejus extrahe, ipso pisce diviso; et cor ejus: quod est primum vivens, et ultimum moriens in animali, secundum Philosophum: et fel et jecur repone tibi in vasculo, pera, seu repositorio. Sunt enim hæc necessaria ad medicamenta utiliter: ut infra describitur. Quod quum fecisset, assavit carnes ejus, hoc est partem corporis piscis, in hospitio. Et sumitur hic caro extense, prout corpus piscis caro vocatur. Unde et Apostolus: Alia, inquit, caro piscium, alia volucrum, alia quadrupedum. Et secum sustulerunt in via. Cetera salierunt, quæ sufficerent eis in via: hoc est, ambobus videbantur sufficere, quum unus eorum nequaquam cibo hujusmodi indigeret; quousque pervenirent in Rages civitatem Medorum.
paras.en: [[6:5|Then the angel said|Tunc dixit angelus]]: [[6:5|Take out the entrails of this fish|Exentera hunc piscem]], that is, draw out its inward parts or entrails, the fish itself being cut open; [[6:5|and lay up his heart|et cor ejus]], which is the first thing living and the last dying in an animal, according to the Philosopher; [[6:5|and his gall, and his liver for thee|et fel et jecur repone tibi]], in a little vessel, a scrip, or some place to keep them. [[6:5|for these are necessary for useful medicines|Sunt enim hæc necessaria ad medicamenta utiliter]], as is described below. [[6:6|And when he had done so, he roasted the flesh thereof|Quod quum fecisset, assavit carnes ejus]], that is, part of the body of the fish, at the inn. And *flesh* is taken here in a wide sense, as the body of a fish is called flesh. Hence the Apostle too says: Another, he says, is the flesh of fishes, another of birds, another of four-footed beasts[[1 Cor 15:39||]] [Denis quotes loosely; the Vulgate has “another of beasts, other of birds, another of fishes”]. [[6:6|and they took it with them in the way|Et secum sustulerunt in via]]. [[6:6|the rest they salted|Cetera salierunt]], [[6:6|as much as might serve them|quæ sufficerent eis]] on the way: that is, it seemed to be enough for both, though one of them had no need at all of such food; [[6:6|till they came to Rages the city of the Medes|quousque pervenirent in Rages civitatem Medorum]].

paras.t: Tunc interrogavit Tobias angelum, et dixit ei: Obsecro te, Azaria frater, ut dicas mihi: Quod remedium habebunt ista, quæ de pisce servare jussisti, videlicet cor, fel, et jecur? Et respondens angelus, dixit ei: Cordis ejus particulam si super carbones ponas, fumus ejus extricat, hoc est, exterminat et repellit, omne genus dæmoniorum, sive a viro, sive a muliere, ita ut ultra non accedat ad eos.
paras.en: [[6:7|Then Tobias asked the angel, and said to him|Tunc interrogavit Tobias angelum, et dixit ei]]: [[6:7|I beseech thee, brother Azarias, tell me|Obsecro te, Azaria frater, ut dicas mihi]]: [[6:7|what remedies are these things good for, which thou hast bid me keep|Quod remedium habebunt ista, quæ de pisce servare jussisti]] of the fish, namely the heart, the gall and the liver? [[6:8|And the angel, answering, said to him: If thou put a little piece of its heart upon coals, the smoke thereof driveth away|Et respondens angelus, dixit ei: Cordis ejus particulam si super carbones ponas, fumus ejus extricat]], that is, banishes and repels, [[6:8|all kind of devils, either from man or from woman, so that they come no more to them|omne genus dæmoniorum, sive a viro, sive a muliere, ita ut ultra non accedat ad eos]].

paras.t: Circa hoc in Scholastica historia dicitur: Nec super hoc mirari debemus, quum fumus cujusdam arboris adustæ eamdem vim habere dicatur. Verumtamen mirum videtur, qualiter res corporales, viles ac mortuæ, queant ita imprimere in intellectuales incorporeasque substantias, præsertim naturaliter et non miraculose, seu ut instrumenta divinæ potentiæ, sicut de igne gehennæ credimus circa spiritus condemnatos. Itaque circa hoc dicunt quidam doctores catholici, sicut et S. Thomas, quod si juxta doctrinam Platonicorum, dæmones essent animalia corpore aeria, animo passiva, mente rationalia, tempore æterna, ut dixit Apuleius, mirum non esset quod corporalia eis imprimerent. Sed quia tenemus quod sunt immateriales, separatæ substantiæ, materialia in eos non imprimunt: et sic fumus piscis non habuisset vim expellendi dæmonium. Propter quod dicunt, quod et facta angeli circa Tobiam figuralia erant, et quod per incensionem fumigationemque cordis et jecoris piscis, figurabantur fervor atque devotio orationis Tobiæ et Saræ conjugis ejus, quorum meritis angelus expulit et religavit dæmonium. Unde infra angelus dicitur hoc fecisse, non fumus. Sicque fumus per significationem, non per impressionem seu influentiam, exterminavit dæmonium.
paras.en: On this the Scholastic History says: Nor ought we to wonder at this, since the smoke of a certain tree, when burnt, is said to have the same power. Yet it seems a wonder how bodily things, base and dead, can so make an impression on intellectual and incorporeal substances, and above all naturally, and not miraculously, that is, as instruments of the divine power, as we believe of the fire of hell in regard to the damned spirits. And so on this point certain catholic doctors, St Thomas among them, say that if, according to the teaching of the Platonists, demons were animals aerial in body, passible in soul [that is, subject to passions], rational in mind, eternal in time, as Apuleius said, it would be no wonder that bodily things made an impression on them. But since we hold that they are immaterial, separate substances, material things make no impression on them: and so the smoke of the fish would not have had the power to drive out the devil. For this reason they say that the angel's doings with Tobias were figurative too, and that by the burning and smoking of the fish's heart and liver were figured the fervour and devotion of the prayer of Tobias and of Sara his wife, by whose merits the angel drove out and bound the devil. Hence below the angel is said to have done this[[Tob 8:3||]], not the smoke [the margin reads Tob. vi, 3; the passage is Tob 8:3]. And thus the smoke drove out the devil by signifying, not by impression or influence.

paras.t: Sed his objici potest, quod gemmæ quædam et herbæ miras et magnas habent virtutes, et impressionem causant in animas rationales, sicut in libris de Proprietatibus rerum describitur; per quarum etiam allationem atque præsentiam dæmones ab obsessis recedunt: quod tamen aliqui dicunt dæmones facere sponte et ficte, ut teneant homines in errore. Aliqui vero dicunt, quod ad humiliandum superbiam dæmonum, Deus sic subdidit eos impressionibus et viribus corporalium ac vilium creaturarum. De his scribit diffuse Guillelmus Parisiensis in libro de Universo: imo de his in diversis codicibus valde multa et diversa leguntur, quæ hic pro nunc tantumdem tetigisse sufficiat.
paras.en: But against this it may be objected that certain gems and herbs have wonderful and great virtues, and cause an impression on rational souls, as is described in the books On the Properties of Things; and when they are brought near and are present, demons even depart from the possessed: which some, however, say the demons do of their own accord and in pretence, to keep men in error. But others say that, to humble the pride of the demons, God has so subjected them to the impressions and powers of bodily and base creatures. William of Paris writes of these things at length in his book On the Universe; indeed very many and various things are read about them in various books, which it may suffice to have touched on this much here for now.

paras.t: Et fel piscis istius valet ad ungendos oculos unctione curativa, in quibus fuerit albugo: ita quod materiam illam feculentam, lumen visuale a suo actu impedientem, expellit. Ideo subditur, et sanabuntur. Multæ enim vires valde potentes, secretæ atque mirificæ in rebus naturalibus inveniuntur, multo plus quam scire valemus.
paras.en: [[6:9|And the gall|Et fel]] of this fish [[6:9|is good for anointing the eyes|valet ad ungendos oculos]] with a healing anointing, [[6:9|in which there is a white speck|in quibus fuerit albugo]]: so that it drives out that foul matter which keeps the sight from its act. Therefore it is added, [[6:9|and they shall be cured|et sanabuntur]]. For many very powerful forces, hidden and wonderful, are found in natural things, far more than we are able to know.

paras.t: Et dicit ei Tobias: Ubi vis ut maneamus? Respondensque angelus ait: Est hic, id est in territorio isto et in oppido quo propinquamus, Raguel nomine, vir propinquus de tribu tua, tribu videlicet Nephthali. Et hic habet filiam nomine Saram; sed neque masculum, neque feminam ullam habet aliam præter illam. Tibi debetur omnis substantia ejus, ex præordinatione divina per connubium contrahendum a te cum filia ejus, et oportet te eam accipere conjugem. Pete ergo eam a patre ejus, et dabit tibi eam uxorem.
paras.en: [[6:10|And Tobias said to him: Where wilt thou that we lodge?|Et dicit ei Tobias: Ubi vis ut maneamus?]] [[6:11|And the angel answering, said|Respondensque angelus ait]]: [[6:11|Here is one|Est hic]], that is, in this territory and in the town we are drawing near to, [[6:11|whose name is Raguel, a near kinsman of thy tribe|Raguel nomine, vir propinquus de tribu tua]], namely the tribe of Nephthali. [[6:11|and he hath a daughter named Sara, but he hath no son nor any other daughter beside her|Et hic habet filiam nomine Saram; sed neque masculum, neque feminam ullam habet aliam præter illam]]. [[6:12|All his substance is due to thee|Tibi debetur omnis substantia ejus]], by divine preordinance, through the marriage to be contracted by thee with his daughter, [[6:12|and thou must take her to wife|et oportet te eam accipere conjugem]]. [[6:13|Ask her therefore of her father, and he will give her thee to wife.|Pete ergo eam a patre ejus, et dabit tibi eam uxorem]]

paras.t: Respondit Tobias et dixit: Audio quia tradita est septem viris, et mortui sunt. Sed et hoc audivi, quia dæmonium occidit illos. Timeo ergo ne forte et mihi hæc eveniant, quæ scilicet evenerunt septem viris quos habuit, dæmoniumque occidit; et quum sim unicus parentibus meis, deponam senectutem illorum parentum meorum cum tristitia ad inferos, id est, occasio fiam per mortem meam, quod parentes mei ex tristitia moriantur, et descendant in limbum.
paras.en: [[6:14|Tobias answered, and said|Respondit Tobias et dixit]]: [[6:14|I hear that she hath been given to seven husbands, and they all died|Audio quia tradita est septem viris, et mortui sunt]]. [[6:14|moreover I have heard, that a devil killed them|Sed et hoc audivi, quia dæmonium occidit illos]]. [[6:15|Now I am afraid, lest the same thing should happen to me also|Timeo ergo ne forte et mihi hæc eveniant]], that is, what befell the seven husbands she had, whom the devil killed; [[6:15|and whereas I am the only child of my parents, I should bring down their old age|et quum sim unicus parentibus meis, deponam senectutem illorum]] (that is, of my parents) [[6:15|with sorrow to hell|cum tristitia ad inferos]]: that is, I shall become by my death the occasion of my parents dying of sorrow and going down to limbo.

paras.t: Tunc angelus dixit ei: Audi me, et ostendam tibi, id est, docebo te, qui sunt quibus prævalere potest dæmonium, ita quod non compescitur virtute angelica aut divina a læsione humana.
paras.en: [[6:16|Then the angel|Tunc angelus]] [[6:16|said to him: Hear me|dixit ei: Audi me]], [[6:16|and I will shew thee|et ostendam tibi]], that is, I will teach thee, [[6:16|who they are, over whom the devil can prevail|qui sunt quibus prævalere potest dæmonium]], so that he is not restrained by angelic or divine power from harming men.

paras.t: Hi namque qui conjugium ita suscipiunt, ut Deum a se et a mente sua excludant, hoc intendendo formaliter: quod pauci directe formaliterque intendunt: vel intendendo hoc concomitanter et æquivalenter, puta voluptatem carnalem prædominantem, ad quam sequitur recessus caritatis et gratiæ Dei ab homine: quam voluptatem multi intendunt. Unde subjungitur: et suæ libidini ita vacent, sicut equus: qui est animal valde luxuriosum, juxta illud Ezechielis, Sicut fluxus equorum fluxus eorum; et mulus: qui etsi non generet, tamen carnis expetit voluptatem; quibus non est intellectus: habet super eos potestatem dæmonium. Non tamen semper permittitur omnes tales occidere, sed tempore desuper præordinato punit eos, nisi pœniteant. Ex quibus verbis elici potest, cur multi post initum conjugium celeriter moriantur.
paras.en: [[6:17|For they who in such manner receive matrimony, as to shut out God from themselves, and from their mind|Hi namque qui conjugium ita suscipiunt, ut Deum a se et a mente sua excludant]], intending this formally, which few intend directly and formally; or intending it concomitantly and equivalently, that is, intending carnal pleasure as what rules them, upon which follows the departure of charity and of God's grace from man: and this pleasure many intend. Hence it is added: [[6:17|and to give themselves to their lust, as the horse|et suæ libidini ita vacent, sicut equus]], which is a very lustful animal, according to that of Ezechiel: [[Ezech 23:20|whose issue as the issue of horses|Sicut fluxus equorum fluxus eorum]]; [[6:17|and mule|et mulus]], which, though it does not beget, yet seeks the pleasure of the flesh; [[6:17|which have not understanding|quibus non est intellectus]]: [[6:17|over them the devil hath power|habet super eos potestatem dæmonium]]. Yet the devil is not always permitted to kill all such men, but at a time ordained from above he punishes them, unless they repent. From these words it may be gathered why many die soon after entering into marriage.

paras.t: Tu autem, qui multitudinem carnalium et stultorum (quorum infinitus est numerus) sequi non debes, quum acceperis eam in uxorem per verba de præsenti, et prout moris tunc erat, ingressus cubiculum, per tres dies naturales, qui noctes includunt, continens esto ab ea, et nihil aliud ages, nisi orationi vacabis cum ea: non quod infra hoc triduum aliud prorsus non egerint quam orare; nam et interim comederunt, et dormierunt, secundum quod infra habetur. Idcirco per istam exclusionem non nisi carnalis copula excludi videtur; et quod interim principalis amborum actio, esset oratio fervens et pura, etsi non continua, tamen assidua: a qua etiam carnalis commixtio illa, quamvis legitima, non mediocriter impedit. Propter quod Apostolus dixit: Nolite fraudare invicem, nisi forte ex consensu ad tempus, ut vacetis orationi.
paras.en: [[6:18|But thou|Tu autem]], who oughtest not to follow the multitude of the carnal and the foolish (whose number is infinite[[Eccles 1:15||]]), [[6:18|when thou shalt take her|quum acceperis eam]] to wife by words of the present [that is, by consent given in words of the present tense, which makes a marriage, as against a promise to marry in the future], and as the custom then was, [[6:18|go into the chamber|ingressus cubiculum]], [[6:18|for three days|per tres dies]] natural, that is, days that include the nights, [[6:18|keep thyself continent from her|continens esto ab ea]], [[6:18|and give thyself to nothing else but to prayers with her|et nihil aliud ages, nisi orationi vacabis cum ea]]: not that within these three days they did nothing whatever but pray, for in the meantime they also ate and slept, as is had below. So by this exclusion nothing but carnal intercourse seems to be excluded; and it means that in the meantime the chief activity of both was to be prayer, fervent and pure, if not continual, yet constant: and that carnal union, though lawful, is no small hindrance to it. For this reason the Apostle said: [[1 Cor 7:5|Defraud not one another, except, perhaps, by consent, for a time, that you may give yourselves to prayer|Nolite fraudare invicem, nisi forte ex consensu ad tempus, ut vacetis orationi]].

paras.t: Ipsa autem nocte, scilicet prima nocte, qua cum ea in cubiculo fueris orans, incenso jecore piscis, fugabitur ab ea dæmonium, potius potestate angelica ac merito vestræ orationis ac continentiæ, quam fumo jecoris inflammati. Quocirca inquiritur, qualiter nunc dicat, Incenso jecore, quum supra jam dixerit, Cordis ejus particulam, etc. Ad quod respondetur, quod utriusque incensio, figurativa et suo modo effectiva fuit expulsionis dæmonii, et utrumque creditur incendisse Tobias. Nam et infra legitur jecur sic incendisse.
paras.en: [[6:19|And on that night|Ipsa autem nocte]], namely the first night, in which thou shalt be with her in the chamber praying, [[6:19|lay the liver of the fish on the fire|incenso jecore piscis]], [[6:19|and the devil shall be driven away|fugabitur ab ea dæmonium]] from her, rather by angelic power and the merit of your prayer and continence than by the smoke of the burning liver. Hence it is asked how he now says, [[6:19|lay the liver of the fish on the fire|Incenso jecore]], when he has already said above, [[6:8|If thou put a little piece of its heart|Cordis ejus particulam]], etc. To which the answer is that the burning of both was a figure, and in its own way a cause, of the driving out of the devil, and Tobias is believed to have burnt both. For below it is read that he burnt the liver in this way[[Tob 8:2||]].

paras.t: Secunda vero nocte in copulatione sanctorum Patriarcharum admitteris, id est, paulatim proficiendo, virtute protractæ orationis promereberis participationem et communionem sanctitatis ac pudicitiæ Patriarcharum sanctorum, hoc est virtutem et gratiam imitandi sanctimoniam, pudicitiamque illorum.
paras.en: [[6:20|But the second night thou shalt be admitted into the society of the holy Patriarchs|Secunda vero nocte in copulatione sanctorum Patriarcharum admitteris]], that is, advancing little by little, by the power of prolonged prayer thou shalt merit a share and communion in the holiness and chastity of the holy Patriarchs: that is, the virtue and grace to imitate their holiness and chastity.

paras.t: Tertia vero nocte benedictionem consequeris, id est, fecunditatem mereberis, et benediceris a Deo, ut filii ex vobis procreentur incolumes. Unde et infra legitur, septem filios genuisse, filiam nullam. Aliqui tamen exponunt istud de benedictione, quam (ut dicunt) præstabat tunc aliquis sacerdos, aut major quis inter ipsos, vices gerens sacerdotis.
paras.en: [[6:21|And the third night thou shalt obtain a blessing|Tertia vero nocte benedictionem consequeris]], that is, thou shalt merit fruitfulness, and be blessed by God, [[6:21|that sound children may be born of you|ut filii ex vobis procreentur incolumes]]. Hence below too it is read that he begot seven sons[[Tob 14:5||]], and no daughter. Some, however, explain this of the blessing which (as they say) some priest used to give at that time, or someone of higher standing among them, acting in the priest's stead.

paras.t: Transacta autem tertia nocte, accipies virginem, consummando cum ea conjugium per carnalem copulam, scilicet quarta nocte, cum timore Domini, ne contingat te circa actum matrimonii aliquo modo excedere, sicut intimoratis contingit: prout supra magis expositum est; et amore filiorum, ad Dei cultum enutriendorum, magis quam libidine ductus, imo omnem libidinosum excludendo amorem pro posse, ut in semine Abrahæ, id est in conjuge tua quæ vera est Abrahæ filia; vel, In semine Abrahæ, id est inter filios Israel, qui semen sunt Abrahæ: vel, In semine Abrahæ, id est in sobole tibi præstanda; benedictionem, id est gratiam salubris fecunditatis, in filiis consequaris: quia et hoc majus est donum, filios procreare quam filias. Aut certe, In semine Abrahæ, id est in Christo, de quo in Genesi ait Dominus ad Abraham: Benedicentur in semine tuo omnes gentes terræ; benedictionem in filiis consequaris, quatenus filii tui per fidem Christi venturi salventur: sicque benedicaris a Domino, non in persona propria tantum, sed item in tua posteritate.
paras.en: [[6:22|And when the third night is past, thou shalt take the virgin|Transacta autem tertia nocte, accipies virginem]], consummating the marriage with her by carnal union, namely on the fourth night, [[6:22|with the fear of the Lord|cum timore Domini]], lest it befall thee to go beyond measure in any way in the act of marriage, as befalls those who do not fear God, as was set out more fully above [a margin note here cannot be read; *above* seems to point to v. 17]; [[6:22|moved rather for love of children|et amore filiorum]], to be brought up for the worship of God, [[6:22|than for lust|magis quam libidine ductus]], indeed shutting out every lustful love as far as thou canst, [[6:22|that in the seed of Abraham|ut in semine Abrahæ]], that is, in thy wife, who is a true daughter of Abraham; or, [[6:22|in the seed of Abraham|In semine Abrahæ]], that is, among the children of Israel, who are the seed of Abraham; or, [[6:22|in the seed of Abraham|In semine Abrahæ]], that is, in the offspring to be given thee, [[6:22|thou mayst obtain a blessing|benedictionem]], that is, the grace of a wholesome fruitfulness, [[6:22|in children|in filiis consequaris]]: for this too is the greater gift, to beget sons rather than daughters. Or else, [[6:22|in the seed of Abraham|In semine Abrahæ]], that is, in Christ, of whom the Lord says to Abraham in Genesis: [[Gen 22:18|in thy seed shall all the nations of the earth be blessed|Benedicentur in semine tuo omnes gentes terræ]]; [[6:22|thou mayst obtain a blessing in children|benedictionem in filiis consequaris]], inasmuch as thy sons are saved through faith in the Christ who is to come: and so thou mayest be blessed by the Lord, not in thy own person only, but also in thy posterity.

paras.t: Mystice ex isto docemur capitulo, quemadmodum angeli sancti multiplex officium circa homines habeant, et multiplicia beneficia eis impendant, atque a corporalibus quoque periculis eripiant eos frequenter. Insuper, qualiter fideles debeant ad matrimonia contrahenda accedere. Et quamvis non obligentur per noctes tres post initum conjugium continere, tenentur tamen contrahere magis desiderio prolis ad Dei obsequium nutriendæ, vel incontinentiæ evitandæ, quam voluptatis venereæ. Et ante contractionem connubii debent se per orationes et sacramentalem confessionem parare ad assumendum Matrimonii sacramentum, quatenus consequantur in ejus contractione et consecratione gratiam sacramentalem, per quam de cetero secundum exigentiam matrimonii conversentur: quia in sacramentis evangelicæ legis gratia continetur et datur dispositis. Cum filiali quoque timore Dei, non cum libidine sensuali contrahendum est ipsum conjugium, ut impleatur quod ait Apostolus: Honorabile connubium et torus immaculatus. Sed, heu! multi quasi equus et mulus, quibus non est intellectus, contoralem accedunt: quam cum prædominante concupiscentia accedere, est mortale, quum sit limites matrimonii omnino excedere. Propter quod omnis amator ardentior perhibetur adulter.
paras.en: In the mystical sense we are taught by this chapter how the holy angels have a manifold office towards men, and bestow manifold benefits on them, and often rescue them from bodily dangers too; and, further, how the faithful ought to approach the contracting of marriage. And though they are not bound to keep continence for three nights after entering into marriage, yet they are bound to contract it more from desire of offspring to be brought up for the service of God, or of avoiding incontinence, than of venereal pleasure. And before the contracting of marriage they ought to prepare themselves by prayers and sacramental confession for receiving the sacrament of Matrimony, so that in its contracting and consecration they may obtain sacramental grace, by which they may thenceforth live as marriage requires: for in the sacraments of the law of the Gospel grace is contained, and is given to those who are disposed for it. With filial fear of God, too, and not with sensual lust, is marriage itself to be contracted, that what the Apostle says may be fulfilled: [[Heb 13:4|Marriage honourable|Honorabile connubium]] [[Heb 13:4|and the bed undefiled|et torus immaculatus]]. But alas! many approach their wife [[6:17|as the horse and mule, which have not understanding|quasi equus et mulus, quibus non est intellectus]]: and to approach her with concupiscence ruling is a mortal sin, since it is to go wholly beyond the bounds of marriage. For this reason every too ardent lover is called an adulterer [that is, of his own wife: the saying is cited by Jerome, Against Jovinian, book 1].

paras.t: Postremo, juxta allegoriam, junior quoque Tobias figura fuit Christi, quem famulati sunt angeli, secundum quod ait Joannes: Videbitis angelos ascendentes et descendentes super Filium hominis. Et sicut Tobias mansit juxta fluvium velocissimum Tigris, sic Filius Dei incarnatus commoratus est juxta nostræ mortalitatis abyssum celerrime et incessabiliter defluentem. Quemadmodum etiam Tobias voluit pedes lavare, sic Christus exivit a Patre, ut suos lavaret electos a sordibus vitiorum in sanguine suo et fonte Baptismi. Circa quod loquitur Beda: Dum Christus lavaret in cruce pedes suos qui ambulaverunt super terram, advenit diabolus, quærens si quid peccati inveniret in eo. Isidorus quoque: Piscis, inquit, voluit devorare Tobiam, et diabolus per suos satellites procuravit occidi Christum.
paras.en: Lastly, according to the allegory, the younger Tobias too was a figure of Christ, whom the angels served, according to what John says: [[John 1:51|you shall see|Videbitis]] [[John 1:51|the angels of God ascending and descending upon the Son of man|angelos ascendentes et descendentes super Filium hominis]]. And as Tobias lodged by the most swift river Tigris, so the Son of God made flesh dwelt by the abyss of our mortality, which flows away most swiftly and without ceasing. As also Tobias wished to wash his feet, so Christ went out from the Father to wash his elect from the filth of their vices in his own blood and in the font of Baptism. On which Bede says: While Christ was washing on the cross his feet, which walked upon the earth, the devil came, seeking whether he might find any sin in him. Isidore too: The fish, he says, wished to devour Tobias, and the devil through his henchmen brought it about that Christ was slain.

paras.t: Denique Tobias timuit piscem, invocavitque angelum: sic Christus ad ostendendum in se veritatem humanæ naturæ, naturali timore ex prævia deliberatione expavit mortem, apparuitque ei angelus corroborans eum, id est per modum confortantis se habens, consolatoria verba loquendo. Quemadmodum demum Tobias piscem traxit in siccum et exenteravit, ejusque interiora pro medicinalibus reservavit: sic Christus vicit diabolum, et ejus patefecit versutias pro informatione fidelium. Et sicut Tobias assavit carnes piscis, et inde refectus est; sic Dominus et Salvator credentes in se igne tribulationis, ardoreque Spiritus Sancti exussit ac consolidavit. Postremo, sicut Tobiam secutus est canis, sic Christum ordo prædicatorum, qui in Scripturis signantur nomine canum, juxta illud: Lingua canum tuorum ex inimicis ab ipso.
paras.en: Then, Tobias feared the fish and called upon the angel: so Christ, to show in himself the truth of human nature, with natural fear, by a deliberate choice made beforehand, was afraid of death, [[Luke 22:43|and there appeared to him an angel|apparuitque ei angelus]] strengthening him, that is, bearing himself as one who comforts, by speaking words of consolation. As, then, Tobias drew the fish onto dry land and gutted it, and kept its inward parts for medicines: so Christ overcame the devil, and laid bare his wiles for the instruction of the faithful. And as Tobias roasted the flesh of the fish, and was refreshed by it, so our Lord and Saviour has burnt through and made firm those who believe in him with the fire of tribulation and the heat of the Holy Ghost. Lastly, as the dog followed Tobias, so the order of preachers follows Christ, who in the Scriptures are signified by the name of dogs, according to that: [[Ps 67:24|the tongue of thy dogs be red with the same|Lingua canum tuorum ex inimicis ab ipso]] [in the Latin, “the tongue of thy dogs, from the enemies, from the same”].

7.title: Declaratio capituli septimi: Ingressi sunt autem ad Raguelem
7.title_en: Explanation of the seventh chapter: And they went in to Raguel

paras.t: Qualiter Tobias cum Sara contraxit conjugium, hic narratur.
paras.en: Here it is told how Tobias contracted marriage with Sara.

paras.t: Ingressi sunt autem ad Raguelem, et suscepit eos cum gaudio. Nam fuit vir bonus, exemplo Abrahæ patris sui, hospitalitati intentus. Intuensque Tobiam Raguel, dixit Annæ uxori suæ: Quam similis est juvenis iste consobrino meo Tobiæ seniori! Fuit equidem Tobias junior similis valde patris sui in vultu et moribus. Et quum hæc dixisset, ait: Unde estis, o juvenes, fratres nostri? Consideravit enim ex habitu, quod erant Israelitæ. Dixerunt ei: Ex tribu Nephthali sumus, ex captivitate Ninive: quod verificatur de ambobus, juxta modum loquendi, quo aliquid attribuitur societati, quia convenit uni seu parti ipsius, ut dictum est. Dixitque illis Raguel: Nostis Tobiam fratrem meum? Qui dixerunt: Novimus.
paras.en: [[7:1|And they went in to Raguel|Ingressi sunt autem ad Raguelem]], [[7:1|and Raguel received them with joy|et suscepit eos cum gaudio]]. For he was a good man, intent on hospitality after the example of Abraham his father[[Gen 18:2||]] [the margin is hard to read here; it seems to give Gen. xviii with the verses following, Abraham's welcome of the three men]. [[7:2|And Raguel looking upon Tobias, said to Anna his wife|Intuensque Tobiam Raguel, dixit Annæ uxori suæ]]: [[7:2|How like is this young man to my cousin|Quam similis est juvenis iste consobrino meo]], the elder Tobias! For the younger Tobias was indeed very like his father in face and in manners. [[7:3|And when he had spoken these words, he said|Et quum hæc dixisset, ait]]: [[7:3|Whence are ye young men our brethren?|Unde estis, o juvenes, fratres nostri?]] For he saw from their dress that they were Israelites. They said to him: [[7:4|We are of the tribe of Nephtali, of the captivity of Ninive|Ex tribu Nephthali sumus, ex captivitate Ninive]]: which is said truly of both of them by that manner of speaking whereby something is ascribed to a company because it belongs to one member, or part, of it, as has been said [that is, it was true of Tobias, and is said of the two together]. [[7:5|And Raguel said to them: Do you know Tobias my brother?|Dixitque illis Raguel: Nostis Tobiam fratrem meum?]] [[7:5|And they said: We know him|Qui dixerunt: Novimus]].

paras.t: Cumque multa bona loqueretur de eo, dixit angelus ad Raguelem: Tobias de quo interrogas, pater istius est. Et misit se Raguel, id est, extendit ad amplectendum, et cum lacrimis osculatus est eum; et plorans super collum ejus ex abundantia lætitiæ et pietatis commotione interna ac viscerosa (quemadmodum Jacob et Joseph cum lacrimis se amplexatos, et super collum alterutrum flevisse leguntur), dixit: Benedictio sit tibi, fili mi, id est, benedicaris a Deo, et ab hominibus commenderis, qui et bona tibi imprecentur: quia boni in naturalibus, et optimi in gratuitis viri filius es. Et Anna uxor ejus, et Sara filia ipsorum lacrimatæ sunt ex eisdem causis quibus Raguel.
paras.en: [[7:6|And when he was speaking many good things of him|Cumque multa bona loqueretur de eo]], [[7:6|the angel said to Raguel|dixit angelus ad Raguelem]]: [[7:6|Tobias concerning whom thou inquirest is this young man's father|Tobias de quo interrogas, pater istius est]]. [[7:7|And Raguel went to him|Et misit se Raguel]] [literally, *sent himself*], that is, stretched himself out to embrace him, [[7:7|and kissed him with tears|et cum lacrimis osculatus est eum]]; [[7:7|and weeping upon his neck|et plorans super collum ejus]] from the abundance of his joy and from an inward and heartfelt stirring of family affection (as Jacob and Joseph are read to have embraced with tears and wept upon each other's neck[[Gen 46:29||]]), [[7:7|said: A blessing be upon thee, my son|dixit: Benedictio sit tibi, fili mi]], that is, mayest thou be blessed by God and commended by men, who also wish thee good things: [[7:7|because thou art the son of a good and most virtuous man|quia boni et optimi viri filius es]], that is, of a man good in the gifts of nature and most excellent in the gifts of grace. [[7:8|And Anna his wife, and Sara their daughter wept|Et Anna uxor ejus, et Sara filia ipsorum lacrimatæ sunt]], for the same reasons as Raguel.

paras.t: Postquam autem locuti sunt, præcepit Raguel occidi arietem et parari convivium. Quumque hortaretur eos discumbere ad prandium, Tobias dixit ex informatione angeli: Hic ego hodie non manducabo neque bibam, nisi prius petitionem meam confirmes, et promittas mihi dare Saram filiam tuam. Raphael quoque prædixit Tobiæ, quod Raguel acquiesceret in hoc. Sic et in Genesi servus Abrahæ, proposito sibi cibo, dixit matri Rebeccæ et Laban: Non comedam donec loquar sermones meos.
paras.en: [[7:9|And after they had spoken|Postquam autem locuti sunt]], [[7:9|Raguel commanded a sheep to be killed, and a feast to be prepared|præcepit Raguel occidi arietem et parari convivium]]. [[7:9|And when he desired them to sit down to dinner|Quumque hortaretur eos discumbere ad prandium]], [[7:10|Tobias said|Tobias dixit]], as the angel had instructed him: [[7:10|I will not eat nor drink here this day, unless thou first grant me my petition, and promise to give me Sara thy daughter|Hic ego hodie non manducabo neque bibam, nisi prius petitionem meam confirmes, et promittas mihi dare Saram filiam tuam]]. Raphael had also foretold to Tobias that Raguel would consent to this. So too in Genesis the servant of Abraham, when food was set before him, said to Rebecca's mother and to Laban: [[Gen 24:33|I will not eat, till I tell my message|Non comedam donec loquar sermones meos]].

paras.t: Quo audito verbo, Raguel expavit ex timore periculi, sciens quid evenerit illis septem viris, qui ingressi sunt ad eam; et timere cœpit, ne forte et huic similiter contingeret. Et quum nutaret, id est, ambigeret quid esset respondendum ac faciendum in casu isto, et non daret ullum petenti responsum: quia pro utraque parte habuit motiva fortissima, nec vidit quid amplius expediret. Grave etenim sibi fuit tam virtuoso juveni et suo cognato filiam denegare, cui secundum legem fuerat danda: et nihilo minus grave fuit tam juvenem illum quam ejus parentes periculo tanto exponere, quod aliis septem viris filiæ suæ contigerat. Dixit ei angelus: Noli timere dare eam isti, quoniam huic timenti Deum debetur conjux filia tua, tam ex ordinatione divina, quam ex lege Mosaica, et propter amborum virtutes. Nam sicut Tobias suis virtutibus meruit tam virtuosam acquirere contoralem, sic Sara tam virtuosum maritum, juxta illud Ecclesiastici: Pars bona, mulier bona; in parte bona timentium Deum dabitur viro pro factis bonis. Et Salomon ait: A Domino datur uxor prudens. Propterea alius non potuit habere illam, quia præordinatio Dei non fallitur neque cassatur.
paras.en: [[7:11|Now when Raguel heard this he was afraid|Quo audito verbo, Raguel expavit]] with fear of the danger, [[7:11|knowing what had happened to those seven husbands, that went in unto her|sciens quid evenerit illis septem viris, qui ingressi sunt ad eam]]; [[7:11|and he began to fear lest it might happen to him also in like manner|et timere cœpit, ne forte et huic similiter contingeret]]; [[7:11|and as he was in suspense|Et quum nutaret]], that is, was in doubt what he ought to answer and to do in this case, [[7:11|and gave no answer to his petition|et non daret ullum petenti responsum]]: because he had the strongest of motives on either side, and did not see which was the more expedient. For it was hard for him to refuse his daughter to so virtuous a young man, his own kinsman, to whom by the law she was to be given; and it was no less hard to expose both that young man and his parents to so great a danger as had befallen his daughter's seven other husbands. [[7:12|The angel said to him|Dixit ei angelus]]: [[7:12|Be not afraid to give her to this man, for to him who feareth God is thy daughter due to be his wife|Noli timere dare eam isti, quoniam huic timenti Deum debetur conjux filia tua]], as much by divine ordinance as by the law of Moses, and because of the virtues of both. For as Tobias by his virtues merited to gain so virtuous a bedfellow [*contoralis*, she who shares the marriage bed], so Sara merited so virtuous a husband, according to that of Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 26:3|A good wife is a good portion, she shall be given in the portion of them that fear God, to a man for his good deeds|Pars bona, mulier bona; in parte bona timentium Deum dabitur viro pro factis bonis]]. And Solomon says: [[Prov 19:14|a prudent wife is properly from the Lord|A Domino datur uxor prudens]]. [[7:12|therefore another could not have her|Propterea alius non potuit habere illam]], because God's foreordaining is neither deceived nor made void.

paras.t: Tunc dixit Raguel: Non dubito quod Deus preces et lacrimas meas admiserit. Et credo quoniam ideo fecit vos venire ad me, ut et ista conjungeretur cognationi, id est viro de tribu sua, secundum legem Moysis, in Numeris, sicut supra expositum est. Denique angelus sanctus cum tanta gravitate et pondere loquebatur, et cum occulta vi tanta in exprimendo et imprimendo, quod ex ejus informatione cor Raguelis fuit subito sic immutatum, confortatum et exhilaratum ex fide et spe. Nam et instanter ac lacrimose Deum rogavit pro filia sua, ut ei provideretur de salubri connubio. Et nunc noli dubium gerere, id est, pro certo agnosce, quod tibi eam tradam.
paras.en: [[7:13|Then Raguel said|Tunc dixit Raguel]]: [[7:13|I doubt not but God hath regarded my prayers and tears|Non dubito quod Deus preces et lacrimas meas admiserit]]. [[7:14|And I believe he hath therefore made you come to me|Et credo quoniam ideo fecit vos venire ad me]], [[7:14|that this maid might be married to one of her own kindred|ut et ista conjungeretur cognationi]], that is, to a man of her own tribe, [[7:14|according to the law of Moses|secundum legem Moysis]], in Numbers[[Num 36:8||]] [the margin gives Num. xxxvi; the verse number cannot be read], as was explained above. Indeed the holy angel spoke with such gravity and weight, and with so great a hidden power in expressing and impressing his words, that through his instruction Raguel's heart was suddenly so changed, strengthened and gladdened by faith and hope. For he too had earnestly and with tears besought God for his daughter, that a wholesome marriage might be provided for her. [[7:14|and now doubt not|Et nunc noli dubium gerere]], that is, know for certain, [[7:14|but I will give her to thee|quod tibi eam tradam]].

paras.t: Et apprehendens dexteram filiæ suæ, dexteræ Tobiæ tradidit, concurrente consensu amborum, et prolatione verborum tunc solitorum, dicens: Deus Abraham et Deus Isaac et Deus Jacob vobiscum sit, per gratiam temporalem et indesinentem, et ipse conjungat vos mente et corpore, conjunctione fructuosa atque fecunda, impleatque benedictionem suam in vobis, præstando vobis incrementa gratiæ et virtutum, deinde salutem æternam. Et accepta charta, fecerunt conscriptionem conjugii, scribendo in charta quæ gerebantur, et dotem puellæ, donumque nuptiale, aut etiam testes. Et post hoc epulati sunt sobrie, benedicentes, id est laudantes, Deum, et gratias ei agentes de conjugio inito; benedicentesque mensam ante comestionem, et postea gratias referentes.
paras.en: [[7:15|And taking the right hand of his daughter, he gave it into the right hand of Tobias|Et apprehendens dexteram filiæ suæ, dexteræ Tobiæ tradidit]], the consent of both concurring, and the words customary at that time being spoken, [[7:15|saying|dicens]]: [[7:15|The God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob be with you|Deus Abraham et Deus Isaac et Deus Jacob vobiscum sit]] by grace in time and without end, [[7:15|and may he join you together|et ipse conjungat vos]] in mind and body, in a fruitful and fertile union, [[7:15|and fulfil his blessing in you|impleatque benedictionem suam in vobis]], by granting you increase of grace and of the virtues, and afterwards eternal salvation. [[7:16|And taking paper they made a writing of the marriage|Et accepta charta, fecerunt conscriptionem conjugii]], writing down on the paper what was done, and the maiden's dowry and the wedding gift, or perhaps also the witnesses. [[7:17|And afterwards they made merry|Et post hoc epulati sunt]], soberly, [[7:17|blessing|benedicentes]], that is, praising, [[7:17|God|Deum]], and giving him thanks for the marriage entered into; and blessing the table before eating, and afterwards returning thanks.

paras.t: Vocavitque ad se Raguel Annam uxorem suam post refectionem, et præcepit ei ut præpararet alterum cubiculum, cubiculo in quo Raguel et uxor ejus jacebant; vel forsan etiam, alterum a cubiculo, in quo priores viri Saræ obierant, ex loci illius horrore. Et introduxit illuc Saram filiam suam post cœnam, et lacrimata est, ex rememoratione præteritarum adversitatum, et ne jam quid tale accideret. Dicitque ei: Forti animo esto, filia mea, id est, firmiter spera in Domino. Deus cæli det tibi gaudium, id est prosperitatem optatam cum viro isto, pro tædio quod perpessa es, id est, eo quod toties es afflicta per mortem virorum priorum, et merito patientiæ tuæ in illis.
paras.en: [[7:18|And Raguel called to him Anna his wife|Vocavitque ad se Raguel Annam uxorem suam]] after the meal, [[7:18|and bade her to prepare another chamber|et præcepit ei ut præpararet alterum cubiculum]], other than the chamber in which Raguel and his wife lay; or perhaps also, other than the chamber in which Sara's former husbands had died, out of horror at that place. [[7:19|And she brought Sara her daughter in thither|Et introduxit illuc Saram filiam suam]] after supper, [[7:19|and she wept|et lacrimata est]], at the remembrance of past adversities, and lest something of the kind should happen now. [[7:20|And she said to her|Dicitque ei]]: [[7:20|Be of good cheer, my daughter|Forti animo esto, filia mea]], that is, hope firmly in the Lord: [[7:20|the Lord of heaven give thee joy|Deus cæli det tibi gaudium]], that is, the prosperity thou desirest with this husband, [[7:20|for the trouble thou hast undergone|pro tædio quod perpessa es]], that is, because thou hast been so often afflicted by the death of thy former husbands, and by the merit of thy patience in those trials.

8.title: Expositio capituli octavi: Postquam vero cœnaverunt, introduxerunt juvenem ad eam
8.title_en: Exposition of the eighth chapter: And after they had supped, they brought in the young man to her

paras.t: Orationes Tobiæ et conjugis ejus hic describuntur.
paras.en: Here are described the prayers of Tobias and of his wife.

paras.t: Postquam vero cœnaverunt, introduxerunt juvenem ad eam, id est ad cubiculum, quo ipsa prius intravit. Recordatus itaque Tobias sermonum angeli, quos de incensione cordis et jecoris piscis narratur dixisse, protulit de cassidili suo, id est repositorio, in quo erant reposita cor, jecur et fel piscis. Et proprie appellatur cassidile, pera facta per modum retis, in qua aucupes ponunt aves captas, et panem pastores. Partem jecoris; posuitque eam super carbones vivos, id est ignitos. Qualiter intelligendum sit istud, supra de incensione cordis piscis patuit. Tunc Raphael angelus apprehendit dæmonium, et religavit eum in desertum superioris Ægypti, ubi de cetero nemini posset nocere: et forsan solo præcepto id egit, vel imperceptibiliter ad momentum se subtraxit, quousque illud explevit, et protinus rediit. Sic in legenda beatissimi Bartholomæi apostoli angelus legitur dæmoni præcepisse ut abiret et maneret, ubi nulli hominum posset nocere.
paras.en: [[8:1|And after they had supped|Postquam vero cœnaverunt]], [[8:1|they brought in the young man to her|introduxerunt juvenem ad eam]], that is, to the chamber which she had entered before. [[8:2|And Tobias remembering the angel's word|Recordatus itaque Tobias sermonum angeli]], which he is told to have spoken about burning the heart and liver of the fish[[Tob 6:8||]], [[8:2|took out of his bag|protulit de cassidili suo]], that is, out of the receptacle in which the heart, liver and gall of the fish had been put away. And a *cassidile* is properly a pouch made in the manner of a net, in which fowlers put the birds they have caught, and shepherds their bread. [[8:2|part of the liver|Partem jecoris]]; [[8:2|and laid it upon burning coals|posuitque eam super carbones vivos]], that is, glowing [*vivos*, literally *living*; Denis glosses it *ignitos*, afire]. How this is to be understood was shown above, on the burning of the fish's heart. [[8:3|Then the angel Raphael took the devil|Tunc Raphael angelus apprehendit dæmonium]], [[8:3|and bound him in the desert of upper Egypt|et religavit eum in desertum superioris Ægypti]], where from then on he could harm no one: and perhaps he did this by a command alone, or withdrew himself imperceptibly for a moment until he had accomplished it, and at once came back. So in the legend of the most blessed apostle Bartholomew an angel is read to have commanded a demon to depart and to remain where it could harm no man.

paras.t: Tunc hortatus est virginem sponsam suam Tobias, dixitque ei: Sara, exsurge mente et corpore, ad devotionem actualem te extendendo, et deprecemur Deum hodie, id est in hac nocte, et cras, id est nocte sequente, et secundum cras, id est etiam tertia nocte: quia istis tribus noctibus Deo jungimur, id est, Deo vacare debemus, ut consequamur tria spiritualia beneficia ab eodem, quæ supra sunt expressa. Tertia autem nocte transacta, videlicet nocte quarta, in nostro erimus conjugio, illud per carnalem copulam consummando. Filii quippe, id est proles, Sanctorum sumus: ut, Filius, non denotet sexum, sed dicat rem genitam, quia sic ambo erant filii Sanctorum, id est devotorum fideliumque parentum seu Patriarcharum. Et non possumus licite ita conjungi per consummationem matrimonii, sicut gentes idololatræ seu indevotæ, quæ ignorant Deum per fidem formatam: ideo sine prævia devotione et oratione carnaliter se cognoscunt.
paras.en: [[8:4|Then Tobias exhorted the virgin|Tunc hortatus est virginem]], his bride, [[8:4|and said to her: Sara, arise|dixitque ei: Sara, exsurge]] in mind and body, stretching thyself out to actual devotion, [[8:4|and let us pray to God to day|et deprecemur Deum hodie]], that is, on this night, [[8:4|and to morrow|et cras]], that is, on the following night, [[8:4|and the next day|et secundum cras]], that is, on the third night too: [[8:4|because for these three nights we are joined to God|quia istis tribus noctibus Deo jungimur]], that is, we ought to give ourselves to God, so as to obtain from him the three spiritual benefits that were set out above[[Tob 6:19||]] [the margin, partly unreadable, seems to give Tob. vi, 19–22, where the angel names what each of the three nights will bring]. [[8:4|and when the third night is over|Tertia autem nocte transacta]], that is, on the fourth night, [[8:4|we will be in our own wedlock|in nostro erimus conjugio]], consummating it by carnal union. [[8:5|For we are the children|Filii quippe]], that is, the offspring, [[8:5|of saints|Sanctorum sumus]]: so that *child* [*filius*, literally *son*] does not denote the sex but means what is begotten, for in this way both were children of saints, that is, of devout and faithful parents, or of the Patriarchs. [[8:5|and we must not be joined together|Et non possumus licite ita conjungi]] lawfully by consummating the marriage, [[8:5|like heathens|sicut gentes]], idolaters or the undevout, [[8:5|that know not God|quæ ignorant Deum]] by formed faith [*fides formata*, faith given its form by charity]: and so they know one another carnally without devotion and prayer going before.

paras.t: Surgentes autem pariter: quo constat quod Tobias sponsam suam hortando, juxta eam paululum sedit: instanter orabant, videlicet ferventer et perseveranter, ambo simul, quatenus communis oratio exaudibilior fieret, dum unius devotio devotioni alterius suffragabatur. Sicque in eis impletum est, quod Dominus universitati in Evangelio ait: Si duo ex vobis super terram consenserint de quacumque re quam petierint, fiet eis a Patre meo. Ubi enim fuerint duo vel tres congregati in nomine meo, ibi in medio eorum sum. Ut sanitas, id est conservatio sanitatis corporalis ac spiritualis, daretur eis, quousque suam complerent periodum.
paras.en: [[8:6|So they both arose|Surgentes autem pariter]]: from which it is plain that Tobias, while exhorting his bride, had sat a little while beside her: [[8:6|and prayed earnestly|instanter orabant]], that is, fervently and perseveringly, [[8:6|both together|ambo simul]], so that their common prayer might be the more readily heard, while the devotion of the one helped the devotion of the other. And so there was fulfilled in them what the Lord says to all in the Gospel: [[Matt 18:19|if two of you shall consent upon earth, concerning anything whatsoever they shall ask, it shall be done to them by my Father|Si duo ex vobis super terram consenserint de quacumque re quam petierint, fiet eis a Patre meo]]. [[Matt 18:20|For where there are two or three gathered together in my name, there am I in the midst of them|Ubi enim fuerint duo vel tres congregati in nomine meo, ibi in medio eorum sum]]. [[8:6|that health|Ut sanitas]], that is, the preservation of bodily and spiritual health, [[8:6|might be given them|daretur eis]], until they should complete their course.

paras.t: Dixitque Tobias, orans Deum cum laudibus: quod est efficacissimum ad impetrandum, juxta quod scriptum est: Laudans invocabo Dominum, et ab inimicis meis salvus ero. Domine, Deus patrum nostrorum, benedicant te cæli et terra et mare et fontes et flumina, et omnes creaturæ tuæ quæ in eis sunt. Porro inanimata et irrationalia Creatorem suum materialiter benedicunt, id est, sua dispositione, natura et consistentia ipsum esse laudabilem monstrant: et considerantibus materiam incitamentumque præbent laudandi Altissimum, cujus bonitas, sapientia, omnipotentia in ipsis relucent, sicut causa in suo effectu. Sic et in Psalmo cantamus: Laudent illum cæli et terra, mare et omnia reptilia in eis. Et tres Pueri in sui hymni exordio cecinerunt: Benedicite, omnia opera Domini, Domino; laudate et superexaltate eum in sæcula. Tu fecisti Adam de limo terræ quantum ad corpus, juxta illud, Formavit Deus hominem de limo terræ: et dedisti ei adjutorium ad prolificandum, Evam: prout in Genesi inducitur: Dixit Dominus Deus, Non est bonum hominem esse solum, faciamus ei adjutorium simile sibi.
paras.en: [[8:7|And Tobias said|Dixitque Tobias]], praying to God with praises, which is most effective for obtaining what we ask, according to what is written: [[Ps 17:4|Praising, I will call upon the Lord: and I shall be saved from my enemies|Laudans invocabo Dominum, et ab inimicis meis salvus ero]]. [[8:7|Lord God of our fathers, may the heavens and the earth, and the sea, and the fountains, and the rivers, and all thy creatures that are in them, bless thee|Domine, Deus patrum nostrorum, benedicant te cæli et terra et mare et fontes et flumina, et omnes creaturæ tuæ quæ in eis sunt]]. Now inanimate and irrational things bless their Creator materially, that is, by their disposition, nature and constitution they show him to be worthy of praise; and to those who consider them they give matter and incitement for praising the Most High, whose goodness, wisdom and omnipotence shine forth in them, as a cause in its effect. So too we sing in the Psalm: [[Ps 68:35|Let the heavens and the earth praise him; the sea, and every thing that creepeth therein|Laudent illum cæli et terra, mare et omnia reptilia in eis]]. And the three Children sang at the beginning of their hymn: [[Dan 3:57|All ye works of the Lord, bless the Lord: praise and exalt him above all for ever|Benedicite, omnia opera Domini, Domino; laudate et superexaltate eum in sæcula]]. [[8:8|Thou madest Adam of the slime of the earth|Tu fecisti Adam de limo terræ]] as to his body, according to that: [[Gen 2:7|the Lord God formed man of the slime of the earth|Formavit Deus hominem de limo terræ]]; [[8:8|and gavest him Eve for a helper|et dedisti ei adjutorium ad prolificandum, Evam]], a helper in begetting offspring, as is related in Genesis: [[Gen 2:18|And the Lord God said: It is not good for man to be alone: let us make him a help like unto himself|Dixit Dominus Deus, Non est bonum hominem esse solum, faciamus ei adjutorium simile sibi]].
