paras.t: Et nunc, Domine, tu scis, quia non luxuriæ causa accipio sororem meam, id est sponsam hanc mihi propinquam cognatione, fidei religione, amore, connubio ac natura specifica; sed sola posteritatis dilectione, in qua, et a qua posteritate, benedicatur nomen tuum in sæcula sæculorum: ita ut posteri nostri te jugiter benedicant, tamque devoti et honesti consistant, ut universi eos considerantes, te in tuis ministris collaudent, eo quod tantam eis contuleris gratiam. Dixit itaque Sara: Miserere nostri, Domine, miserere nostri. Repetitio illa fuit fervoris indicium. Et consenescamus ambo pariter sani, sanitate mentis et corporis. Nam et sani corpore, ceteris paribus, aptiores sunt Deo servire quam ægri.
paras.en: [[8:9|And now, Lord, thou knowest|Et nunc, Domine, tu scis]], [[8:9|that not for fleshly lust do I take my sister|quia non luxuriæ causa accipio sororem meam]], that is, this bride, near to me in kindred, in the religion of faith, in love, in wedlock and in specific nature [that is, as sharing one and the same human nature], [[8:9|but only for the love of posterity|sed sola posteritatis dilectione]], [[8:9|in which|in qua]], and from which posterity, [[8:9|thy name may be blessed for ever and ever|benedicatur nomen tuum in sæcula sæculorum]]: so that our descendants may bless thee continually, and be so devout and upright that all who see them may praise thee in thy servants, because thou hast bestowed such grace on them. [[8:10|Sara also said|Dixit itaque Sara]]: [[8:10|Have mercy on us, O Lord, have mercy on us|Miserere nostri, Domine, miserere nostri]]. That repetition was a sign of fervour. [[8:10|and let us grow old both together in health|Et consenescamus ambo pariter sani]], health of mind and of body. For those who are healthy in body are, other things being equal, more fit to serve God than the sick.

paras.t: Et factum est circa pullorum cantum, scilicet in confinio noctis atque auroræ, quum adhuc tenebræ essent, accersiri, id est vocari, jussit Raguel servos suos, et abierunt cum eo pariter ut foderent sepulcrum. Sicque corruerat Raguel magna ex parte a spe sua, qua dixisse legitur superius: Non dubito quod Deus preces et lacrimas meas admiserit; et credo quod ideo fecit vos venire ad me, etc. Solent equidem homines vacillare a spe arduorum, instante hora qua percepturi sunt, quid in tali casu evenerit. Ex nimio enim desiderio rei cupitæ, verentur contraria. Dicebat enim: Ne forte simili modo evenerit ei, quod et ceteris aliis septem viris, qui sunt ingressi ad eam. Quumque parassent fossam, regressus Raguel ad uxorem suam, dixit: Mitte unam ex ancillis tuis, et videat si, id est an, mortuus sit, ut sepeliam eum antequam illucescat dies: ne cognita morte ejus, augeatur confusio nostra. At illa misit unam ex ancillis: quæ, scilicet ancilla, ingressa cubiculum latenter, reperit eos salvos et incolumes, secum pariter dormientes. Non puto quod nudi condormiebant in lecto uno; sed post fatigationem ex diuturna oratione, ploratione, vigilia, reclinaverunt se cum veste ad repausandum.
paras.en: [[8:11|And it came to pass about the cockcrowing|Et factum est circa pullorum cantum]], that is, at the border of night and dawn, while it was still dark, [[8:11|Raguel ordered his servants to be called for|accersiri jussit Raguel servos suos]], [[8:11|and they went with him together to dig a grave|et abierunt cum eo pariter ut foderent sepulcrum]]. So Raguel had in great part fallen away from his hope, in which he is read above to have said: [[Tob 7:13|I doubt not but God hath regarded my prayers and tears|Non dubito quod Deus preces et lacrimas meas admiserit]]; [[Tob 7:14|And I believe he hath therefore made you come to me|et credo quod ideo fecit vos venire ad me]], etc. For men are wont to waver in their hope of hard things when the hour is at hand in which they are to learn what has come about in such a case: from too great a desire for the thing longed for, they fear the contrary. [[8:12|For he said|Dicebat enim]]: [[8:12|Lest perhaps it may have happened to him, in like manner as it did to the other seven husbands, that went in unto her|Ne forte simili modo evenerit ei, quod et ceteris aliis septem viris, qui sunt ingressi ad eam]]. [[8:13|And when they had prepared the pit|Quumque parassent fossam]], [[8:13|Raguel went back to his wife, and said|regressus Raguel ad uxorem suam, dixit]]: [[8:14|Send one of thy maids, and let her see if he be dead|Mitte unam ex ancillis tuis, et videat si, id est an, mortuus sit]], [[8:14|that I may bury him before it be day|ut sepeliam eum antequam illucescat dies]]: lest, if his death becomes known, our shame be increased. [[8:15|So she sent one of her maidservants|At illa misit unam ex ancillis]]: [[8:15|who went into the chamber|quæ, scilicet ancilla, ingressa cubiculum]] (the maid, that is) secretly, [[8:15|and found them safe and sound, sleeping both together|reperit eos salvos et incolumes, secum pariter dormientes]]. I do not think that they slept naked in one bed; but after the weariness of long prayer, weeping and watching, they lay down in their clothes to rest.

paras.t: Quæ reversa, nuntiavit bonum nuntium. Et benedixerunt Dominum Raguel et Anna uxor ejus, gratias ei agendo de conservatione Tobiæ in vita, et dixerunt: Benedicimus te, Domine, Deus Israel, quia non contigit nobis quemadmodum putabamus. Fecisti enim nobiscum misericordiam tuam, hoc est, effectum pietatis tuæ nobis in hac re, et in aliis multis exhibuisti; et exclusisti a nobis inimicum persequentem nos, scilicet invisibilem hostem diabolum, qui viros alios nostræ filiæ occidendo, nos quoque dire afflixit, contristavit et diffamavit. Misertus es autem duobus unicis, scilicet unico filio senioris Tobiæ, et unicæ filiæ nostræ. Fac eos, Domine, plenius benedicere te, ut sint tibi quotidie gratiores, et sacrificium laudis tuæ et suæ sanitatis offerre: ita ut spiritualiter offerant tibi laudes pro sacrificio legis, et pro beneficio sanitatis suæ, id est concessæ eis a te, gratias referant tibi; ut cognoscat universitas gentium, ad quarum notitiam ista devenerint, quia tu es Deus solus in universa terra.
paras.en: [[8:16|And returning she brought the good news|Quæ reversa, nuntiavit bonum nuntium]]: [[8:16|and Raguel and Anna his wife blessed the Lord|Et benedixerunt Dominum Raguel et Anna uxor ejus]], giving him thanks that Tobias had been kept alive, and [[8:17|said|dixerunt]]: [[8:17|We bless thee, O Lord God of Israel|Benedicimus te, Domine, Deus Israel]], [[8:17|because it hath not happened as we suspected|quia non contigit nobis quemadmodum putabamus]]. [[8:18|For thou hast shewn thy mercy to us|Fecisti enim nobiscum misericordiam tuam]], that is, thou hast shown us the effect of thy loving-kindness in this matter and in many others; [[8:18|and hast shut out from us the enemy that persecuted us|et exclusisti a nobis inimicum persequentem nos]], namely the invisible foe, the devil, who by killing our daughter's other husbands grievously afflicted, saddened and defamed us too. [[8:19|And thou hast taken pity upon two only children|Misertus es autem duobus unicis]], namely the only son of the elder Tobias and our only daughter. [[8:19|Make them, O Lord, bless thee more fully|Fac eos, Domine, plenius benedicere te]], so that they may be daily more pleasing to thee, [[8:19|and to offer up to thee a sacrifice of thy praise, and of their health|et sacrificium laudis tuæ et suæ sanitatis offerre]]: so that they may spiritually offer thee praises in place of the sacrifice of the law, and return thee thanks for the benefit of their health, that is, the health granted them by thee; [[8:19|that all nations may know|ut cognoscat universitas gentium]] to whose knowledge these things may come, [[8:19|that thou alone art God in all the earth|quia tu es Deus solus in universa terra]].

paras.t: Statimque præcepit servis suis Raguel, ut replerent terra fossam quam fecerant, priusquam illucesceret. Uxori autem suæ dixit ut instrueret, id est pararet, convivium, et præpararet omnia quæ in cibos iter agentibus erant necessaria, eis quos intendebat mittere ad Gabelum, ad quem non volebat Tobiam permittere ire. Nam subditur: Et adjuravit Raguel Tobiam, ut duas hebdomadas moraretur apud se, quatenus interim mutuo adspectu gauderent in Domino. De omnibus autem quæ possidebat Raguel, dimidiam partem dedit Tobiæ. De bonis immobilibus videntur pauca aut nihil habuisse in terra illa aliena. Et fecit hanc scripturam, ut pars dimidia quæ supererat, post obitum eorum Tobiæ dominio deveniret.
paras.en: [[8:20|And immediately Raguel commanded his servants|Statimque præcepit servis suis Raguel]], [[8:20|to fill up the pit they had made|ut replerent terra fossam quam fecerant]] with earth, [[8:20|before it was day|priusquam illucesceret]]. [[8:21|And he spoke to his wife to make ready a feast|Uxori autem suæ dixit ut instrueret convivium]], [[8:21|and prepare all kind of provisions that are necessary for such as go a journey|et præpararet omnia quæ in cibos iter agentibus erant necessaria]], for those whom he meant to send to Gabelus, to whom he would not let Tobias go. For it is added: [[8:23|And Raguel adjured Tobias, to abide with him two weeks|Et adjuravit Raguel Tobiam, ut duas hebdomadas moraretur apud se]], so that meanwhile they might rejoice in the Lord in seeing one another. [[8:24|And of all things which Raguel possessed, he gave one half to Tobias|De omnibus autem quæ possidebat Raguel, dimidiam partem dedit Tobiæ]]. Of immovable goods they seem to have had little or nothing in that foreign land. And he [[8:24|made a writing|fecit hanc scripturam]], [[8:24|that the half that remained should after their decease come also to Tobias|ut pars dimidia quæ supererat, post obitum eorum Tobiæ dominio deveniret]].

paras.t: Textus autem tam planus est, ut immorari non congruat. Sed ex prædictis docentur conjugati fideles, ne instar infidelium absque prævia devotione et oratione conveniant.
paras.en: But the text is so plain that it is not fitting to dwell on it. From what has been said, however, faithful married people are taught not to come together, as unbelievers do, without devotion and prayer going before.

9.title: Elucidatio capituli noni: Tunc vocavit Tobias angelum ad se
9.title_en: Explanation of the ninth chapter: Then Tobias called the angel to him

paras.t: Nunc recitatur qualiter Gabelus adductus, persolvit concessam sibi pecuniam.
paras.en: Here it is related how Gabelus, being brought, paid back the money lent to him.

paras.t: Tunc vocavit Tobias angelum seorsum ad se, quem hominem æstimabat, dixitque ei, recognoscendo beneficia ejus grata et humili mente: Azaria frater, peto ut auscultes verba mea. Si me ipsum tradam tibi servum hereditarium, vel usque ad septimum annum, secundum legem in Exodo fixam, non ero condignus, id est satis gratus, providentiæ tuæ circa me, et beneficiis mihi per providentiam tuam collatis, imo et conjugi meæ et ejus parentibus.
paras.en: [[9:1|Then Tobias called the angel|Tunc vocavit Tobias angelum]] apart [[9:1|to him, whom he took to be a man|ad se, quem hominem æstimabat]], [[9:1|and said to him|dixitque ei]], acknowledging his kindnesses with a grateful and humble mind: [[9:1|Brother Azarias, I pray thee hearken to my words|Azaria frater, peto ut auscultes verba mea]]. [[9:2|If I should give myself to be thy servant|Si me ipsum tradam tibi servum]] for ever [Latin servum hereditarium, a servant for life whose service passes to his heirs], or until the seventh year, according to the law laid down in Exodus[[Ex 21:2||]] [the margin, as read, gives Exod. xiii, 3, which does not fit; the law of release in the seventh year is Ex 21:2], [[9:2|I should not make a worthy return|non ero condignus]], that is, I should not be grateful enough, [[9:2|for thy care|providentiæ tuæ]] over me, and for the benefits bestowed through thy care on me, nay, and on my wife and her parents.

paras.t: Tamen obsecro te, ut adhuc aliquid plus propter me facias, videlicet ut assumas tibi animalia, quæ portent necessaria in itinere, vel te et Gabelum, sive servitia, id est quosdam ex servis Raguelis, qui sint socii itineris tui, et vadas ad Gabelum in Rages civitatem Medorum, reddasque ei chirographum suum, et recipias ab eo pecuniam, et roges eum venire ad nuptias.
paras.en: [[9:3|However, I beseech thee|Tamen obsecro te]] to do something more still for my sake, namely [[9:3|to take with thee beasts|ut assumas tibi animalia]] to carry what is needed on the journey, or to carry thee and Gabelus, [[9:3|and servants|sive servitia]], that is, some of Raguel's servants, to be companions of thy journey, [[9:3|and to go to Gabelus to Rages the city of the Medes|et vadas ad Gabelum in Rages civitatem Medorum]]: [[9:3|and to restore to him his note of hand, and receive of him the money, and desire him to come to my wedding|reddasque ei chirographum suum, et recipias ab eo pecuniam, et roges eum venire ad nuptias]].

paras.t: Jam dictum est supra: Eadem die contigit, ut Sara filia Raguelis in Rages civitate Medorum audiret improperium. Si ergo et Gabelus habitavit in Rages civitate Medorum, in eadem urbe manebant Raguel et Gabelus? Ad hoc multipliciter respondetur. Primo, quod erant duæ urbes ejusdem nominis, sicut in aliquibus regnis sunt plura oppida sive villagia idem nomen habentia. Secundo, quod Rages non solum est nomen urbis, sed etiam provinciæ, sicut Samaria interdum est nomen urbis regni decem tribuum, quandoque patriæ: sicque unus istorum habitavit in urbe sic dicta, alter in civitate provinciæ sic vocatæ. Tertio, quod supra textus correctus sic habet: Contigit ut Sara filia Raguelis in civitate Medorum. Primæ autem responsioni consonare videtur quod supra Raphael ait: Mansi apud Gabelum fratrem nostrum qui moratur in Rages civitate Medorum, quæ posita est in monte Ecbatanis: quod addi videtur, ad differentiam alterius Rages.
paras.en: It has already been said above: [[Tob 3:7|it happened on the same day, that Sara daughter of Raguel, in Rages a city of the Medes, received a reproach|Eadem die contigit, ut Sara filia Raguelis in Rages civitate Medorum audiret improperium]]. If, then, Gabelus too lived in Rages, the city of the Medes, did Raguel and Gabelus live in the same city? To this several answers are given. First, that there were two cities of the same name, as in some kingdoms there are several towns or villages having the same name. Second, that Rages is the name not only of a city but also of a province, as Samaria is sometimes the name of the city of the kingdom of the ten tribes, sometimes of the country: and so one of them lived in the city so called, the other in a city of the province so named. Third, that above, the corrected text reads thus: It happened that Sara the daughter of Raguel, in a city of the Medes[[Tob 3:7||]] [that is, without the name Rages; the Douay-Rheims, following the Clementine Vulgate, has “in Rages a city of the Medes”]. Now with the first answer seems to agree what Raphael says above: [[Tob 5:8|I have abode with Gabelus our brother, who dwelleth at Rages a city of the Medes, which is situate in the mount of Ecbatana|Mansi apud Gabelum fratrem nostrum qui moratur in Rages civitate Medorum, quæ posita est in monte Ecbatanis]]: which seems to be added to distinguish it from the other Rages.

paras.t: Scis enim, quoniam numerat pater meus dies absentiæ meæ. Et si tardavero uno die plus, contristabitur anima ejus. Et certe vides quomodo adjuravit me Raguel, cujus adjuramentum spernere non possum. Specialiter sollicitus fuit de patre, magis compatiens ei propter ipsius cæcitatem et sanctitatem.
paras.en: [[9:4|For thou knowest that my father numbereth the days|Scis enim, quoniam numerat pater meus dies]] of my absence. [[9:4|and if I stay one day more, his soul will be afflicted|Et si tardavero uno die plus, contristabitur anima ejus]]. [[9:5|And indeed thou seest how Raguel hath adjured me, whose adjuring I cannot despise|Et certe vides quomodo adjuravit me Raguel, cujus adjuramentum spernere non possum]]. He was especially anxious about his father, having the more compassion on him because of his blindness and his holiness.

paras.t: Tunc Raphael assumens quatuor ex servis Raguelis, ut eos ædificaret et informaret in via, et decenter comitatus veniret, magisque sibi crederetur, et duos camelos, forsan unum pro adducendo Gabelo, alium pro se, non ob sui indigentiam, sed condecentiam, in Rages perrexit. Et inveniens Gabelum, dedit ei chirographum suum, et recepit omnem pecuniam. Indicavitque ei de Tobia filio Tobiæ omnia quæ gesta sunt. Fecitque eum, puta Gabelum, secum venire ad nuptias convivii Tobiæ.
paras.en: [[9:6|Then Raphael took four of Raguel's servants|Tunc Raphael assumens quatuor ex servis Raguelis]], to edify and instruct them on the way, and so that he might come fittingly attended and be the more believed, [[9:6|and two camels|et duos camelos]], perhaps one for bringing Gabelus, the other for himself, not because he needed it but for seemliness, [[9:6|and went to Rages|in Rages perrexit]]: [[9:6|and finding Gabelus, gave him his note of hand, and received of him all the money|Et inveniens Gabelum, dedit ei chirographum suum, et recepit omnem pecuniam]]. [[9:7|And he told him concerning Tobias the son of Tobias, all that had been done|Indicavitque ei de Tobia filio Tobiæ omnia quæ gesta sunt]]: [[9:7|and made him|Fecitque eum]], that is, Gabelus, [[9:7|come with him to the wedding|secum venire ad nuptias]] feast of Tobias.

paras.t: Et flevit Gabelus præ gaudio, viso et osculato Tobia, benedixitque Deum, et dixit Tobiæ eum benedicendo: Benedicat te Deus Israel, id est, abundantiam spiritualium temporaliumque bonorum tibi gratiose concedat meritis patris tui, quia filius es viri optimi, id est devotissimi Deo, et justi ad proximos, et timentis Deum, et eleemosynas facientis copiosissime, secundum vires suas.
paras.en: [[9:8|and Gabelus wept|Et flevit Gabelus]] for joy, when he had seen and kissed Tobias, [[9:8|and blessed God|benedixitque Deum]], [[9:9|And said|et dixit]] to Tobias, blessing him: [[9:9|The God of Israel bless thee|Benedicat te Deus Israel]], that is, may he graciously grant thee an abundance of goods spiritual and temporal by the merits of thy father, [[9:9|because thou art the son of a very good|quia filius es viri optimi]], that is, most devoted to God, [[9:9|and just man|et justi]] towards his neighbours, [[9:9|and that feareth God, and doth almsdeeds|et timentis Deum, et eleemosynas facientis]] most plentifully, according to his means.

paras.t: Et dicatur benedictio super uxorem tuam, id est, omnes eam noscentes imprecentur ei bona propter virtutes ipsius, et super parentes vestros, ut laudentur propter vestras probitates, fecunditates et virtuositates: quemadmodum mulier prudens beatificavit gloriosissimam Virginem propter Filium ejus dicendo ad Filium: Beatus venter qui te portavit, et ubera quæ suxisti. Et videatis filios vestros, et filios filiorum vestrorum usque in tertiam et quartam generationem, id est, diuturnitatem vitæ, fecunditatemque prolis, et prosperitatem longævam obtineatis a Domino: et sit semen vestrum benedictum a Deo Israel, qui regnat in sæcula sæculorum, id est, a vero Deo benedicatur posteritas vestra. Quid mirum si tam devote locutus est, cum quo angelus sanctus fuit, et ambulavit tam diu, non sine instructione salubri?
paras.en: [[9:10|And may a blessing come upon thy wife|Et dicatur benedictio super uxorem tuam]], that is, may all who know her wish her well because of her virtues, [[9:10|and upon your parents|et super parentes vestros]], that they may be praised for your uprightness, fruitfulness and virtues: as the prudent woman called the most glorious Virgin blessed because of her Son, saying to the Son: [[Luke 11:27|Blessed is the womb that bore thee and the paps that gave thee suck|Beatus venter qui te portavit, et ubera quæ suxisti]]. [[9:11|And may you see your children, and your children's children, unto the third and fourth generation|Et videatis filios vestros, et filios filiorum vestrorum usque in tertiam et quartam generationem]], that is, may you obtain from the Lord length of life, fruitfulness of offspring and long-lasting prosperity: [[9:11|and may your seed be blessed by the God of Israel, who reigneth for ever and ever|et sit semen vestrum benedictum a Deo Israel, qui regnat in sæcula sæculorum]], that is, may your posterity be blessed by the true God. What wonder if he spoke so devoutly, with whom the holy angel had been, and had walked so long, not without wholesome instruction?

paras.t: Cumque omnes dixissent, Amen, id est, sic fiat, accesserunt ad convivium. Sed et cum timore Domini nuptiarum convivium exercebant. Omnes etenim ædificabantur in angelo, quamvis eum hominem esse putabant, quia exemplarissimus fuit in omni apparatu et verbo. Similiter sponsus et sponsa fuerunt timorati. Ideo absque dissolutione, gula, lascivia, ibi omnia agebantur cum gaudio spirituali: quod cunctis est imitandum fidelibus.
paras.en: [[9:12|And when all had said, Amen|Cumque omnes dixissent, Amen]], that is, so be it, [[9:12|they went to the feast|accesserunt ad convivium]]: [[9:12|but the marriage feast they celebrated also with the fear of the Lord|Sed et cum timore Domini nuptiarum convivium exercebant]]. For all were edified by the angel, though they thought him a man, since he was a perfect example in all his bearing and speech. The bridegroom and the bride likewise were God-fearing. So everything was done there without dissipation, gluttony or wantonness, with spiritual joy: which all the faithful should imitate.

10.title: Expositio capituli decimi: Quum vero moras faceret Tobias
10.title_en: Exposition of the tenth chapter: But as Tobias made longer stay

paras.t: Dolor parentum Tobiæ, et reditus ejus hic enarrantur.
paras.en: The grief of the parents of Tobias, and his return, are related here.

paras.t: Quum vero moras redeundi longiores, quam itineratio requirebat, faceret Tobias, causa nuptiarum, propter quas a Raguele detinebatur, sollicitus erat pater ejus, id est inquietus corde præ cura, et anxius, dicens: Putas quare moratur filius meus, etc., et nemo reddet illi pecuniam? Ex nimio enim filii sui amore imaginabatur varias causas dilationis reditus sui, quemadmodum anxiatis moris est; et dicere poterat illud Job: Cogitationes meæ variæ succedunt sibi, et mens in diversa rapitur.
paras.en: [[10:1|But as Tobias made longer stay|Quum vero moras]] in returning, longer than the journey required, [[10:1|upon occasion of the marriage|causa nuptiarum]], for which he was kept back by Raguel, [[10:1|Tobias his father was solicitous|sollicitus erat pater ejus]], that is, restless at heart with care, and anxious, [[10:1|saying|dicens]]: [[10:1|Why thinkest thou doth my son tarry|Putas quare moratur filius meus]], etc., [[10:2|and no man will pay him the money?|et nemo reddet illi pecuniam]] For out of his exceeding love for his son he imagined various causes for the delay of his return, as is the way of anxious men; and he could have said that word of Job: [[Job 20:2|various thoughts succeed one another in me, and my mind is hurried away to different things|Cogitationes meæ variæ succedunt sibi, et mens in diversa rapitur]].

paras.t: Cœperunt autem contristari nimis, ipse Tobias senior, et Anna uxor ejus; et cœperunt flere, eo quod die statuto minime reverteretur filius eorum ad eos. Nam antequam recessit ab eis, computaverunt dies infra quos posset reverti, et apud ipsos reversus consistere: infra quos non fuit reversus.
paras.en: They began [[10:3|to be exceeding sad|contristari nimis]], [[10:3|both he|ipse]], the elder Tobias, [[10:3|and Anna his wife|et Anna uxor ejus]]; and they began [[10:3|to weep|flere]], [[10:3|because their son did not return to them on the day appointed|eo quod die statuto minime reverteretur filius eorum ad eos]]. For before he went away from them, they had reckoned the days within which he could return and be back with them: and within these he had not returned.

paras.t: Flebat ergo mater ejus irremediabilibus lacrimis: sicut et Jacob deflevit filium suum Joseph, nullam consolationem admittens; atque dicebat: Hei mihi, fili mi, ut quid te misimus peregrinari, lumen, id est delectabile et jucundum objectum, oculorum nostrorum: prout hoc supra fuit expositum; baculum senectutis nostræ: quod ibi quoque est explanatum; solatium, id est causa et materia consolationis et gaudii, vitæ nostræ? Delectabile namque est, præsentem habere dilectum et adjutorem, et præsertim filium sapientem, obedientem et virtuosum, juxta illud Proverbiorum: Filius sapiens lætificat patrem. Et rursus: Fili, si sapiens fuerit animus tuus, gaudebit tecum cor meum, et exsultabunt renes mei quum locuta fuerint rectum labia tua. Itemque: Exsultat gaudio pater justi; qui sapientem genuit, lætabitur in eo.
paras.en: Therefore [[10:4|his mother wept|Flebat ergo mater ejus]] with tears past all remedy [Latin irremediabilibus lacrimis, where the Douay-Rheims has “was quite disconsolate”], as Jacob also wept for his son Joseph[[Gen 37:34||]], admitting no consolation[[Gen 37:35||]]; [[10:4|and said|atque dicebat]]: [[10:4|woe is me, my son|Hei mihi, fili mi]]; [[10:4|why did we send thee to go to a strange country|ut quid te misimus peregrinari]], [[10:4|the light|lumen]], that is, the delightful and pleasant object, [[10:4|of our eyes|oculorum nostrorum]], as was expounded above; [[10:4|the staff of our old age|baculum senectutis nostræ]], which was also explained there[[Tob 5:23||]] [the margin gives Tob. v, 23 beside the light of our eyes; that verse has the staff of our old age]; [[10:4|the comfort|solatium]], that is, the cause and matter of consolation and joy, [[10:4|of our life|vitæ nostræ]]? For it is delightful to have one's beloved and helper present, and above all a son who is wise, obedient and virtuous, according to that of the Proverbs: [[Prov 10:1|A wise son maketh the father glad|Filius sapiens lætificat patrem]] [the margin, as read, gives Prov. x, 1; the same words stand at Prov 15:20]. And again: [[Prov 23:15|My son, if thy mind be wise, my heart shall rejoice with thee|Fili, si sapiens fuerit animus tuus, gaudebit tecum cor meum]], [[Prov 23:16|And my reins shall rejoice, when thy lips shall speak what is right|et exsultabunt renes mei quum locuta fuerint rectum labia tua]]. And also: [[Prov 23:24|The father of the just rejoiceth greatly: he that hath begotten a wise son, shall have joy in him|Exsultat gaudio pater justi; qui sapientem genuit, lætabitur in eo]].

paras.t: Spem posteritatis nostræ: quoniam unica proles fuit eorum, qui amplius generare nequibant, ideo eo carere fuit gravissimum. Nam et parentes quodammodo manent in posteris suis. Hinc in Ecclesiastico scriptum est: Mortuus est pater ejus, videlicet boni sapientisque filii, et quasi non est mortuus: similem enim reliquit post se. In vita sua vidit et lætatus est in illo, et in obitu suo non est contristatus. Reliquit enim defensorem domus suæ.
paras.en: [[10:4|the hope of our posterity|Spem posteritatis nostræ]]: because he was their only child, and they could beget no more, to be without him was therefore most grievous. For parents too in a manner live on in their offspring. Hence it is written in Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 30:4|His father is dead|Mortuus est pater ejus]], namely the father of a good and wise son, [[Ecclus 30:4|and he is as if he were not dead: for he hath left one behind him that is like himself|et quasi non est mortuus: similem enim reliquit post se]]. [[Ecclus 30:5|While he lived he saw and rejoiced in him: and when he died he was not sorrowful|In vita sua vidit et lætatus est in illo, et in obitu suo non est contristatus]]. [[Ecclus 30:6|For he left behind him a defender of his house|Reliquit enim defensorem domus suæ]].

paras.t: Omnia, jam prælibata, simul in te uno habentes, non te debuimus dimittere ire a nobis; sed potius nuntium quemdam misisse, ne majus et carius bonum exponeremus periculo propter minus et vilius bonum. Quod aliquo modo sic erat, nisi providentia Dei aliter ordinasset et inspirasset, propter majus bonum ex illa itineratione consecutum, tam Tobiæ juniori, ejusque contorali, quam amborum parentibus: quod femina ista nondum cognovit, sed postea cognito eo gratias egit.
paras.en: [[10:5|We having all things together in thee alone|Omnia, jam prælibata, simul in te uno habentes]] (all the things just named), [[10:5|ought not to have let thee go from us|non te debuimus dimittere ire a nobis]]; but rather to have sent some messenger, lest we should expose a greater and dearer good to danger for the sake of a lesser and cheaper good. And in a manner it was so, had not the providence of God ordained and inspired otherwise, for the sake of the greater good that came of that journey, as much to the younger Tobias and his bride as to the parents of both: which this woman did not yet know, but afterwards, when she knew it, she gave thanks.

paras.t: Cui dicebat Tobias: Tace, et noli turbari. Sanus est filius noster, ut spero. Satis fidelis est vir cum quo misimus eum. Fuit itaque Tobias multo constantior atque prudentior conjuge sua: ideo, tanquam caput ipsius, eam informavit et consolabatur, et ex divina inspiratione sic loquebatur. Deus etenim eum consolabatur secrete intrinsecus.
paras.en: [[10:6|And Tobias said to her|Cui dicebat Tobias]]: [[10:6|Hold thy peace, and be not troubled|Tace, et noli turbari]]: [[10:6|our son is safe|Sanus est filius noster]], as I hope; [[10:6|that man with whom we sent him is very trusty|Satis fidelis est vir cum quo misimus eum]]. Tobias, then, was far steadier and more prudent than his wife: and so, as her head[[Eph 5:23||]], he instructed and comforted her, and spoke thus by divine inspiration. For God was comforting him secretly within.

paras.t: Illa autem nullo modo consolari poterat, sed quotidie exsiliens, circumspiciebat et circumibat vias omnes, per quas spes remeandi videbatur, ut procul videret eum, si fieri posset, venientem.
paras.en: [[10:7|But she could by no means be comforted|Illa autem nullo modo consolari poterat]], [[10:7|but daily running out looked round about, and went into all the ways by which there seemed any hope he might return, that she might if possible see him coming afar off|sed quotidie exsiliens, circumspiciebat et circumibat vias omnes, per quas spes remeandi videbatur, ut procul videret eum, si fieri posset, venientem]].

paras.t: At vero Raguel dicebat ad generum suum, hoc est maritum filiæ suæ, juniorem Tobiam: Mane hic, et ego mittam nuntium salutis tuæ ad patrem tuum, id est virum qui parentibus tuis denuntiet te sanum ac prosperum esse. Cui Tobias ait: Ego novi, quia pater meus et mater mea modo dies computant absentiæ meæ, et cruciatur spiritus, id est anima, eorum in ipsis, videlicet animis amborum.
paras.en: [[10:8|But Raguel said to his son in law|At vero Raguel dicebat ad generum suum]], that is, to the husband of his daughter, the younger Tobias: [[10:8|Stay here, and I will send a messenger|Mane hic, et ego mittam nuntium]] of thy welfare to [[10:8|thy father|patrem tuum]], that is, a man to tell thy parents that thou art safe and prospering. [[10:9|And Tobias said to him|Cui Tobias ait]]: [[10:9|I know that my father and mother now count the days|Ego novi, quia pater meus et mater mea modo dies computant]] of my absence, [[10:9|and their spirit is grievously afflicted|et cruciatur spiritus]], that is, their soul, [[10:9|within them|in ipsis]], namely in the souls of both.

paras.t: Cumque verbis multis rogaret Raguel Tobiam, ut diutius secum maneret: quia dilexit eum ut proprium filium, non solum quoniam gener suus fuit, sed quia tam bonus, et propter virtutes patris sui, et quia cognatus; et ille eum nulla ratione vellet audire, id est nulli persuasioni Raguelis acquiescere, sciens quod parentes sui non contentarentur, nisi eo reverso. Et forsan, quia audierat ab angelo, qualiter fel piscis haberet vim illuminandi oculos per maculam seu albuginem excæcatos, sperabat hoc in patre suo fiendum, sicut jam fuit expertus in conjuge sua de incensione cordis et jecoris piscis. Tradidit ei Saram, et dimidiam partem omnis, id est totius, substantiæ suæ in rebus mobilibus, in pueris, in puellis, id est servis et ancillis, forsan empticiis, in pecudibus, id est ovibus, et camelis, et in vaccis, et pecunia multa.
paras.en: [[10:10|And when Raguel had pressed Tobias with many words|Cumque verbis multis rogaret Raguel Tobiam]] to stay longer with him, because he loved him as his own son, not only because he was his son-in-law, but because he was so good, and for the sake of his father's virtues, and because he was a kinsman; [[10:10|and he by no means would hearken to him|et ille eum nulla ratione vellet audire]], that is, would yield to no persuasion of Raguel, knowing that his parents would not be content until he was back. And perhaps, because he had heard from the angel how the gall of the fish had power to give light to eyes blinded by a spot or white film, he hoped that this would be done in his father, as he had already found in his wife with the burning of the fish's heart and liver. [[10:10|he delivered Sara unto him, and half of all|Tradidit ei Saram, et dimidiam partem omnis]], that is, the whole, [[10:10|his substance|substantiæ suæ]] in movable goods, [[10:10|in menservants, and womenservants|in pueris, in puellis]], that is, male and female slaves, perhaps bought ones, [[10:10|in cattle|in pecudibus]], that is, sheep, [[10:10|in camels, and in kine, and in much money|et camelis, et in vaccis, et pecunia multa]].

paras.t: Et salvum dimisit eum a se, dicens: Angelus Domini sanctus sit in itinere vestro, vos dirigendo ac protegendo: sicut et Tobias oravit quando filium a se dimisit, ut patuit: perducatque vos incolumes, et inveniatis omnia recta circa parentes vestros, et videant oculi mei filios vestros priusquam moriar.
paras.en: [[10:10|and sent him away safe|Et salvum dimisit eum]] from him, [[10:11|Saying|dicens]]: [[10:11|The holy angel of the Lord be with you in your journey|Angelus Domini sanctus sit in itinere vestro]], directing and protecting you, as the elder Tobias also prayed when he sent his son away, as was shown[[Tob 5:21||]] [the margin, as read, gives Tob. v, 31, probably for v, 21, where Tobias prays that God and his angel go with them]: [[10:11|and bring you through safe|perducatque vos incolumes]], [[10:11|and that you may find all things well about your parents, and my eyes may see your children before I die|et inveniatis omnia recta circa parentes vestros, et videant oculi mei filios vestros priusquam moriar]].

paras.t: Et apprehendentes parentes filiam suam, osculati sunt eam: ut moris est in tali recessu. Et dimiserunt ire, monentes eam honorare soceros, id est parentes sui mariti, tanquam proprios parentes, quum maritus et conjux sint una caro; diligere maritum, et ex filiali dilectione eum timere, juxta illud Apostoli: Uxor autem timeat virum. Princeps quoque Apostolorum in prima sua hortatur Canonica: Mulieres subditæ sint viris suis, sicut Sara obediebat Abrahæ, dominum eum vocans. Regere familiam, quantum ad agenda in quotidiano obsequio, præsertim in domo: quæ tanquam minora, potius spectant ad conjugis dispositionem, quæ et potius residet domi. Mariti vero est, exteriora et majora disponere. Gubernare domum, id est sobolem, in directione ad matrem pertinente, ac utensilia domus; et se ipsam irreprehensibilem exhibere, vitando ad minus peccata mortalia et scandala; quatenus qui alios habet regere, increpare, disponere, se in cunctis exhibeat exemplarem, ne ei dicatur, Cura te ipsam.
paras.en: [[10:12|And the parents taking their daughter kissed her|Et apprehendentes parentes filiam suam, osculati sunt eam]], as is the custom at such a parting, [[10:12|and let her go|Et dimiserunt ire]], [[10:13|Admonishing her to honour her father and mother in law|monentes eam honorare soceros]], that is, her husband's parents, as her own parents, since husband and wife are one flesh; [[10:13|to love her husband|diligere maritum]], and to fear him out of filial love, according to that of the Apostle: [[Eph 5:33|And let the wife fear her husband|Uxor autem timeat virum]]. The Prince of the Apostles too exhorts in his first canonical epistle: [[1 Pet 3:1|let wives be subject to their husbands|Mulieres subditæ sint viris suis]], [[1 Pet 3:6|As Sara obeyed Abraham, calling him lord|sicut Sara obediebat Abrahæ, dominum eum vocans]][[Gen 18:12||]] [the margin, as read, gives Gen. xviii, 19; at Gen 18:12 Sara calls Abraham “my lord”]. [[10:13|to take care of the family|Regere familiam]] [Latin regere, to rule], as regards what is to be done in daily service, especially in the house: these things, being lesser, belong rather to the wife's ordering, since she also stays more at home; but it is the husband's part to order the outward and greater things. [[10:13|to govern the house|Gubernare domum]], that is, the children, by the guidance that belongs to the mother, and the furnishings of the house; [[10:13|and to behave herself irreprehensibly|et se ipsam irreprehensibilem exhibere]], by avoiding at least mortal sins and scandals; so that she who has to rule, rebuke and order others may show herself an example in all things, lest it be said to her: [[Luke 4:23|heal thyself|Cura te ipsam]] [Latin te ipsam, “thyself” in the feminine; the margin, as read, gives Luke 19:23, but the saying is Luke 4:23].

paras.t: Ex his instruuntur parentes, qualiter debeant informare filias suas dum traduntur ad nuptias. Ipsæ quoque conjuges hic docentur, quid ad earum spectet officium, et quam virtuose debeant conversari, præsertim vitando omnia impudicitiæ signa et opera atque femineas inquietudines, loquacitates et levitates, ut sexum vincant virtutibus, conditionemque moribus.
paras.en: From these things parents are taught how they ought to instruct their daughters when they are given in marriage. Wives themselves, too, are taught here what belongs to their duty, and how virtuously they ought to live, above all by avoiding every sign and deed of immodesty, and womanly restlessness, talkativeness and lightness, so that they may surpass their sex by their virtues, and their condition by their conduct.

11.title: Declaratio capituli undecimi: Quumque reverterentur, pervenerunt ad Charan
11.title_en: Explanation of the eleventh chapter: And as they were returning they came to Charan

paras.t: Quumque reverterentur Raphael et Tobias, ejusque uxor cum familia et jumentis, pervenerunt ad Charan, id est oppidum sic vocatum, quod est in medio itinere contra Niniven, id est ex opposito Ninive civitatis, decima die a recessu de domo Raguelis. Hanc Charan dicunt aliqui esse, de qua scriptum est in Actibus: Tunc exiit Abraham de terra Chaldæorum, et habitavit in Charan; quæ in Genesi vocatur Haran. Dixitque angelus: Tobia frater, scis quemadmodum reliquisti patrem tuum, videlicet cæcum, desolatum et inopem. Si placet itaque tibi, præcedamus. Ecce quam humiliter loquitur angelus. Et lento gradu insequantur iter nostrum familia simul cum conjuge tua, et cum animalibus. Quumque hoc placuisset Tobiæ, dixit Raphael ad Tobiam: Tolle tecum de felle piscis, quod alicubi fuit repositum, erit enim necessarium. Tulit itaque Tobias ex felle illo, et abierunt.
paras.en: [[11:1|And as they were returning|Quumque reverterentur]], Raphael and Tobias, and his wife with the household and the beasts, [[11:1|they came to Charan|pervenerunt ad Charan]], that is, a town so called, [[11:1|which is in the midway to Ninive|quod est in medio itinere contra Niniven]], that is, over against the city of Ninive, on the tenth day after leaving Raguel's house [the Vulgate has *undecimo die*, the eleventh day]. Some say that this is the Charan of which it is written in the Acts: [[Acts 7:4|Then he went out of the land of the Chaldeans and dwelt in Charan|Tunc exiit Abraham de terra Chaldæorum, et habitavit in Charan]]; which in Genesis is called Haran[[Gen 11:31||]]. [[11:2|And the angel said|Dixitque angelus]]: [[11:2|Brother Tobias, thou knowest how thou didst leave thy father|Tobia frater, scis quemadmodum reliquisti patrem tuum]], that is, blind, desolate and needy. [[11:3|If it please thee therefore, let us go before|Si placet itaque tibi, præcedamus]] (see how humbly the angel speaks), [[11:3|and let the family follow softly after us, together with thy wife, and with the beasts|Et lento gradu insequantur iter nostrum familia simul cum conjuge tua, et cum animalibus]]. [[11:4|And as this their going pleased him|Quumque hoc placuisset Tobiæ]], [[11:4|Raphael said to Tobias: Take with thee of the gall of the fish|dixit Raphael ad Tobiam: Tolle tecum de felle piscis]], which had been put away somewhere, [[11:4|for it will be necessary|erit enim necessarium]]. [[11:4|So Tobias took some of that gall and departed|Tulit itaque Tobias ex felle illo, et abierunt]].

paras.t: Anna autem sedebat secus viam quotidie in supercilio montis, unde respicere poterat de longinquo. Et dum ex eodem loco specularetur adventum ejus, vidit a longe, et illico cognovit venientem filium suum. Nuntiavitque viro suo.
paras.en: [[11:5|But Anna sat beside the way daily, on the top of a hill, from whence she might see afar off|Anna autem sedebat secus viam quotidie in supercilio montis, unde respicere poterat de longinquo]]. [[11:6|And while she watched his coming from that place|Et dum ex eodem loco specularetur adventum ejus]], [[11:6|she saw him afar off|vidit a longe]], [[11:6|and presently perceived it was her son coming|et illico cognovit venientem filium suum]]; and [[11:6|she told her husband|Nuntiavitque viro suo]].

paras.t: Dixitque Raphael ad Tobiam: At ubi introieris domum tuam, id est domum tuæ habitationis, statim adora Dominum Deum tuum. Et gratias agens ei. Unde elicitur, quod de longe redeuntes, et a suis negotiationibus revertentes, mox ut domum suam intraverint, debeant in primis Deum adorare, et gratias ei referre pro beneficiis sibi in via ab eo exhibitis. Accede ad patrem tuum, et osculare eum, pro consolatione ipsius ex caritate sincera: juxta quod Paulus apostolus frequenter in suis scribit epistolis, Salutate invicem in osculo sancto. Statimque lini, id est inunge, super oculos ejus ex felle isto. Scias enim quoniam mox aperientur oculi ejus ad videndum ut ante: puta post mediam horam, ut paulo post tangitur. Et videbit pater tuus lumen cæli. Natura namque operatur successive. Et poterat angelus divina virtute absque naturali medicamine cæcum illuminare; sed ad gloriam Creatoris voluit creaturæ vires ostendere, et ne præsumamus Deum tentare, quærendo supernaturale auxilium, dum habemus per naturam subsidium. Et in adspectu tuo gaudebit.
paras.en: [[11:7|And Raphael said to Tobias|Dixitque Raphael ad Tobiam]]: [[11:7|As soon as thou shalt come into thy house|At ubi introieris domum tuam]], that is, the house where thou dwellest, [[11:7|forthwith adore the Lord thy God|statim adora Dominum Deum tuum]]: [[11:7|and giving thanks to him|Et gratias agens ei]]. From this it is drawn that those who come back from afar, returning from their business, ought, as soon as they have entered their house, first of all to adore God and give him thanks for the benefits he has shown them on the way. [[11:7|go to thy father, and kiss him|Accede ad patrem tuum, et osculare eum]], for his consolation, out of sincere charity: according to what the apostle Paul often writes in his epistles: [[Rom 16:16|Salute one another with an holy kiss|Salutate invicem in osculo sancto]][[1 Cor 16:20||]][[1 Thess 5:26||]] [the margin here is partly unreadable; it seems to cite Rom. xvi, 16, 1 Cor. xvi, 20 and 1 Thess. v, 26]. [[11:8|And immediately anoint his eyes with this gall of the fish|Statimque lini, id est inunge, super oculos ejus ex felle isto]]. [[11:8|For be assured that his eyes shall be presently opened|Scias enim quoniam mox aperientur oculi ejus]] to see as before: that is, after half an hour, as is touched on a little later. [[11:8|and thy father shall see the light of heaven|Et videbit pater tuus lumen cæli]]. For nature works by degrees. The angel could have given the blind man light by divine power without a natural remedy; but for the glory of the Creator he willed to show the powers of the creature, and also that we should not presume to tempt God by seeking supernatural help while we have assistance through nature. [[11:8|and shall rejoice in the sight of thee|Et in adspectu tuo gaudebit]].

paras.t: Tunc præcucurrit canis, qui simul fuerat in via, et quasi nuntius adveniens, blandimento suæ caudæ gaudebat. Et consurgens cæcus pater, cœpit, offendens, id est impingens pedibus, currere, ex amore filii redeuntis, et ex gaudio de reditu ejus; et data manu sua puero dirigenti viam ipsius, occurrit obviam filio suo, et osculatus est eum cum uxore sua, id est tam ipse quam uxor sua Anna mater Tobiæ. Quumque adorassent Deum Tobias et ejus parentes, et gratias egissent de reditu. Quo constat, quod domestici suscipientes redeuntem debeant simul cum illo Dominum adorare, et gratias agere. Consederunt, ad conferendum de peractis in via et expeditione negotii.
paras.en: [[11:9|Then the dog, which had been with them in the way, ran before|Tunc præcucurrit canis, qui simul fuerat in via]], [[11:9|and coming as if he had brought the news|et quasi nuntius adveniens]], [[11:9|shewed his joy by his fawning and wagging his tail|blandimento suæ caudæ gaudebat]]. [[11:10|And his father that was blind, rising up|Et consurgens cæcus pater]], [[11:10|began to run stumbling with his feet|cœpit offendens pedibus currere]] [*offendens*, stumbling, which Denis explains as *impingens*, striking against things] out of love for his returning son and joy at his return; [[11:10|and giving a servant his hand|et data manu sua puero]], who guided his way, [[11:10|went to meet his son|occurrit obviam filio suo]], and [[11:11|kissed him, as did also his wife|osculatus est eum cum uxore sua]], that is, both he and his wife Anna, the mother of Tobias. [[11:12|And when they had adored God|Quumque adorassent Deum]], Tobias and his parents, [[11:12|and given him thanks|et gratias egissent]] for his return. From this it is clear that the household, receiving one who returns, ought to adore the Lord together with him and give thanks. [[11:12|they sat down together|Consederunt]], to talk over what had been done on the way and the carrying through of the business.

paras.t: Tunc sumens Tobias de felle piscis, linivit oculos patris sui. Et sustinuit, id est exspectavit, quasi dimidiam fere horam effectum inunctionis illius; et cœpit albugo, id est subtilis tenuisque materia fæculenta instar pelliculæ, ut est in alis vespertilionis, quasi membrana, id est pellicula ovi, ex oculis ejus egredi. Quam apprehendens Tobias junior, traxit ab oculis ejus, videlicet patris sui, statimque visum recepit. Nam lumen visuale manserat in pupilla. Porro, cæcum a nativitate, in cujus oculis non est lumen hujusmodi, videntem efficere, excedit virtutem totius naturæ creatæ: quod Christus et multi Sancti post eum Ecclesiæ filii peregerunt, nullusque antea legitur peregisse. Propter quod cæcus a nativitate a Christo illuminatus, dixit incredulis: A sæculo non est auditum, quia aperuit quis oculos cæci nati.
paras.en: [[11:13|Then Tobias taking of the gall of the fish, anointed his father's eyes|Tunc sumens Tobias de felle piscis, linivit oculos patris sui]]. [[11:14|And he stayed|Et sustinuit]], that is, waited, [[11:14|about half an hour|quasi dimidiam fere horam]] for the effect of that anointing: [[11:14|and a white skin began|et cœpit albugo]], that is, a fine, thin and dreggy matter like a little skin, such as there is on the wings of a bat, [[11:14|like the skin|quasi membrana]], that is, the thin skin [[11:14|of an egg|ovi]], [[11:14|to come out of his eyes|ex oculis ejus egredi]]. [[11:15|And Tobias took hold of it, and drew it from his eyes|Quam apprehendens Tobias junior, traxit ab oculis ejus]], that is, his father's, [[11:15|and recovered his sight|statimque visum recepit]]. For the light of sight had remained in the pupil. But to make one blind from birth, in whose eyes there is no such light, to see, exceeds the power of all created nature: this Christ did, and many Saints, sons of the Church, after him, and no one is read to have done it before. For this reason the man born blind, given light by Christ, said to the unbelievers: [[John 9:32|From the beginning of the world it hath not been heard, that any man hath opened the eyes of one born blind|A sæculo non est auditum, quia aperuit quis oculos cæci nati]].

paras.t: Et glorificabant, id est, gloriosum, omnipotentem, pium esse fatebantur, Deum, ipse Tobias et uxor ejus, et omnes qui sciebant eum, id est fideles qui noverant eum, vel etiam quidam gentilium. Dixitque Tobias: Benedico te, Domine, Deus Israel, quoniam tu castigasti me. Nam humilis Tobias reputavit sibi plagam cæcitatis pro suis evenisse peccatis: quæ tamen ob alias causas evenerat. Nihilo minus etiam ad purgationem venialium culparum Tobiæ potuit contigisse, et sic fuit non solum exercitatio atque probatio justi, sed et castigatio aliqualiter rei. Et tu salvasti, id est curasti, me de hujusmodi plaga: juxta illud Job, Percutit, et manus ejus sanabunt. Sicque in Tobia impletum est quod ad Hebræos fertur: Omnis disciplina in præsenti videtur non esse gaudii, sed mœroris; postea autem fructum pacatissimum exercitatis per eam reddet justitiæ. Et vidit Tobias filium suum.
paras.en: [[11:16|And they glorified|Et glorificabant]], that is, they confessed to be glorious, almighty and loving, [[11:16|God, both he|Deum, ipse]], Tobias, [[11:16|and his wife and all that knew him|et uxor ejus, et omnes qui sciebant eum]], that is, the faithful who knew him, or even some of the gentiles. [[11:17|And Tobias said|Dixitque Tobias]]: [[11:17|I bless thee, O Lord God of Israel, because thou hast chastised me|Benedico te, Domine, Deus Israel, quoniam tu castigasti me]]. For the humble Tobias reckoned that the plague of blindness had come upon him for his sins, though it had come about for other reasons. Nevertheless it could also have befallen Tobias for the cleansing of venial faults, and so it was not only the exercise and proving of a just man, but also in some measure the chastisement of one at fault. [[11:17|and thou hast saved me|Et tu salvasti, id est curasti, me]], that is, cured me of such a plague: according to that of Job: [[Job 5:18|he striketh, and his hands shall heal|Percutit, et manus ejus sanabunt]]. And so there was fulfilled in Tobias what is said to the Hebrews: [[Heb 12:11|all chastisement for the present indeed seemeth not to bring with it joy, but sorrow: but afterwards it will yield to them that are exercised by it the most peaceable fruit of justice|Omnis disciplina in præsenti videtur non esse gaudii, sed mœroris; postea autem fructum pacatissimum exercitatis per eam reddet justitiæ]]. And Tobias saw his son.

paras.t: Ingressa est etiam domum Tobiæ senioris post septem dies Sara uxor filii ejus, et omnis familia et pecora sana, et cameli, et pecunia multa uxoris: sed et illa pecunia, quam receperat a Gabelo. Dicuntque aliqui, ideo Raphaelem suggessisse Tobiæ ut præcederent, quatenus Tobias senior curaretur antequam uxor filii ejus intraret, ne inveniretur ab ea et a venientibus secum, in pristina paupertate, cæcitate et indispositione. Vel ideo præcessum suggessit, ut justo desolato celerius impenderetur solatium, et etiam afflictissimæ matri Tobiæ.
paras.en: [[11:18|And after seven days Sara his son's wife and all the family arrived safe, and the cattle|Ingressa est etiam domum Tobiæ senioris post septem dies Sara uxor filii ejus, et omnis familia et pecora sana]], [[11:18|and the camels, and an abundance of money of his wife's|et cameli, et pecunia multa uxoris]]: [[11:18|and that money also which he had received of Gabelus|sed et illa pecunia, quam receperat a Gabelo]]; all these came into the house of the elder Tobias. Some say that Raphael suggested to Tobias that they should go ahead so that the elder Tobias might be cured before his son's wife came in, lest he be found by her, and by those who came with her, in his former poverty, blindness and ill state. Or he suggested going ahead so that comfort might be brought the sooner to the desolate just man, and also to Tobias's most afflicted mother.

paras.t: Et narravit parentibus suis omnia beneficia Dei, quæ fecisset circa eum per hominem, id est angelum in specie hominis apparentem, qui eum duxerat. Veneruntque Achior et Nabath consobrini Tobiæ, et etiam alii quidam contribules et vicini ipsius, ad ipsum Tobiam, congratulantes ei de omnibus bonis quæ circa illum ostenderat Deus, id est beneficiis sibi desuper exhibitis in se ipso et in filio suo. Et per septem dies epulantes omnes cum sobrietate, et cum gaudio magno in Domino, gavisi sunt. Et forsan introierunt ad Tobiam, antequam uxor filii ejus advenit, quamvis hoc postea recitetur. Mox enim ut perceperunt eum illuminatum, venerunt. Epulationem autem potuerunt differre usque ad ingressum uxoris filii ejus.
paras.en: [[11:19|And he told his parents all the benefits of God, which he had done to him by the man|Et narravit parentibus suis omnia beneficia Dei, quæ fecisset circa eum per hominem]], that is, the angel appearing in the form of a man, [[11:19|that conducted him|qui eum duxerat]]. [[11:20|And Achior and Nabath the kinsmen of Tobias came|Veneruntque Achior et Nabath consobrini Tobiæ]], and also certain others of his tribe and his neighbours, to Tobias himself, [[11:20|and congratulating with him for all the good things that God had done for him|congratulantes ei de omnibus bonis quæ circa illum ostenderat Deus]], that is, for the benefits shown him from above, in himself and in his son. [[11:21|And for seven days they feasted|Et per septem dies epulantes]], all of them soberly, [[11:21|and rejoiced all with great joy|et cum gaudio magno in Domino, gavisi sunt]] in the Lord. And perhaps they came in to Tobias before his son's wife arrived, although this is told afterwards; for as soon as they learned that he had been given his sight, they came. But they could have put off the feasting until his son's wife came in.

paras.t: Postremo, per linitionem fellis piscis, designatur amaritudo veræ contritionis et compunctionis internæ, qua cordis oculi illustrantur, et maculæ vitiorum delentur.
paras.en: Lastly, by the anointing with the fish's gall is signified the bitterness of true contrition and of inward compunction, by which the eyes of the heart are enlightened and the stains of vices are wiped away.

paras.t: Patet quoque ex dictis, qualiter Dominus pauperem facit et ditat, et post dejectionem repente honestat. Idcirco in omni adversitate in ipso tanquam in providissimo atque piissimo patre confidendum est, constanti, fideli, et insuperabili mente, quia certissimum est, eum universa et singula considerare plenissime.
paras.en: It is clear too from what has been said how the Lord [[1 Kings 2:7|maketh poor and maketh rich|pauperem facit et ditat]], and after casting down suddenly brings to honour. Therefore in every adversity we must trust in him as in a most provident and most loving father, with a constant, faithful and unconquerable mind, since it is most certain that he considers all things, and each one of them, most fully.
